title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared combinational radix-4 division with parallel trial subtracts
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline; no LESSONS.md exists and
there are no earlier micro_opt attempts to repeat. The baseline reports
5.442 MHz and an approximately 200 ns, 156-cell worst path through
forwarding and the combinational ALU. The ALU expresses signed and
unsigned division and remainder with separate / and % operators. These
are the strongest candidates for the deep arithmetic path, even when
CoreMark is executing an ordinary integer operation. Shortening this
arithmetic network can raise Fmax without reducing iterations per cycle.

The only recorded experiment is the baseline; no LESSONS.md exists and

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath with one combinational
unsigned radix-4 restoring divider, shared by all four operations. Keep
the ALU interface, execution latency, pipeline, forwarding, bus-stall
behavior, and nret=1 port contract unchanged. Convert signed operands
to unsigned 32-bit magnitudes before the divider and correct quotient
and remainder signs afterward; unsigned operations use operands directly.

Unroll 16 stages, each consuming two dividend bits. Precompute D, 2D,
and 3D once as 34-bit unsigned values. Each stage forms T=4*R+next_two_bits and
computes T-D, T-2D, and T-3D in parallel. Derive the three fit predicates
from the extended subtract results' borrow bits, rather than adding
separate magnitude comparisons. Select the largest fitting multiple
with a small priority encoder and a balanced four-way remainder mux,
and append its two-bit quotient digit. Taper stage widths to the consumed
dividend prefix: stage i, numbered from zero, needs W=2*(i+1) bits for
T and its remainder. Subtract the low W bits of each multiple using
W+1 bits; a candidate fits only if its borrow is zero AND every bit of
that 34-bit multiple above W-1 is zero. This high-bit guard is mandatory,
especially for divisors near UINT_MAX; truncating multiples without it
is incorrect. The width bound follows from the remainder never exceeding
the dividend prefix consumed so far. It avoids unnecessarily full-width
subtracts in early stages. Quotient digits must not form another serial
arithmetic chain. This halves the number of serial quotient decisions;
parallel subtracts cost area but sharing the engine and avoiding separate
comparator chains should make the trade favorable on the Tang Nano 20K.

Explicitly preserve division-by-zero results (quotient all ones and
remainder the original dividend), signed truncation toward zero, the
dividend's sign on signed remainder, and INT_MIN/-1 results (INT_MIN
quotient and zero remainder). Leave every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression
exactly as it is, and exclude the real divider in ALTOPS builds. Leave
multiplication and every RV32I operation unchanged. Validate actual
arithmetic with independent quotient/remainder references and the
existing M-extension tests and cosim; ALTOPS formal alone is insufficient.
Confirm the hypothesis with vendor timing and canonical stalled CoreMark:
expect unchanged marked cycles and improved median Fmax. The main risk
is that three parallel subtracts and their selection routing outweigh
the reduction in serial stages; the expected gain is a timing prediction,
not an already measured result.

A standalone bit-width-accurate arithmetic model of this algorithm passed
40,500 signed/unsigned quotient-and-remainder comparisons against independent
integer arithmetic, including random operands, D/2D/3D boundaries, high-bit
divisors, divide-by-zero, and overflow. This checks the proposed algorithm
and width guards; the implementing RTL still needs the existing eval gates.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the shared combinational radix-4 divider in cores/bench/rtl/alu.sv. DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU use one unsigned magnitude engine with 16 unrolled stages. Stage widths increase from 2 to 32 bits. D, 2D, and 3D are precomputed at 34 bits; each stage performs three parallel W+1-bit subtracts and combines their borrow bits with mandatory guards on every omitted multiple bit. A two-bit priority encoder drives a balanced four-way remainder mux. Each quotient digit drives its own output slice, without a serial quotient arithmetic chain.

Signed operands use 32-bit two's-complement magnitudes and output sign correction. Divide-by-zero explicitly returns an all-ones quotient and the original dividend as remainder. INT_MIN/-1 naturally produces INT_MIN and zero. ALTOPS expressions remain byte-for-byte unchanged, and the real divider is excluded by RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS. Multiplication, RV32I expressions, pipeline latency, forwarding, bus stalls, and the nret=1 interface are unchanged. No architectural deviations from the hypothesis were needed.

Extended cores/bench/test/test_alu.py while retaining every existing test. Independent Python integer references explicitly truncate signed division toward zero and give signed remainder the dividend's sign. New tests check 73,592 directed results around D/2D/3D boundaries and every tapered width, high-bit divisors, unsigned maxima, all signed operand combinations, zero divisors, and overflow; another 20,480 results use a fixed random seed with both full-width and small divisors. All 26 cocotb ALU tests passed.

Local formal status: PASS on the first attempt, 53 checks passed and 0 failed. Command: RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh. It selected wrapper_si.sv and checks_si.cfg automatically. No counterexamples or formal fix attempts occurred. This is the ALTOPS gate; real arithmetic was validated separately by the 94,072 new cocotb comparisons and cosimulation. The slow formal-deep suite was not run.

Lint passed without warnings in both real-arithmetic and ALTOPS configurations using core_pkg.sv first, as the existing Makefile and tool flows require. The prompt's literal alphabetical *.sv lint command encounters the baseline's compilation-unit typedef ordering dependency (core.sv precedes core_pkg.sv). The equivalent package-first check, make lint TARGET=bench, passed; no unrelated source-order edits were made.

NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench passed: every selftest retirement matched the Python ISS both with and without randomized instruction/data stalls, and canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC and UART validation. NRET=1 is supplied because the direct Makefile cosim build defaults to two retirement channels, while this core declares one.

make timing TARGET=bench passed the Gowin vendor flow. NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench then passed all three placement options and canonical stalled CoreMark. Fmax values were 5.544, 5.680, and 5.680 MHz; median Fmax is 5.680 MHz versus the recorded baseline's 5.442 MHz, a 4.37% improvement. Marked CoreMark cycles remained exactly 4,491,485 for 10 iterations. Fitness rose from 12.12 to 12.65 iterations/second. Gowin logic cells fell from 12,312 to 4,932; registers remained 460, LUT-RAM 8, BSRAM 6, and DSP 6.

The timing gain is modest despite the large area reduction. The option-0 worst path still crosses forwarding and the divider, with 185.670 ns arrival versus the baseline's 199.837 ns. Its path contains 249 cells and 164 reported logic levels versus the baseline's 156 cells and 150 levels, so parallel subtract and selection routing remain material costs. The measured median improves, but the divider still dominates timing and the arithmetic tests are finite rather than an exhaustive 32-bit proof.
lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r1s0 (regression, +4.37%): Sharing DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU in a tapered radix-4 divider reduced logic cells by 60%, but parallel trial-subtract selection and routing kept division on the forwarding-to-ALU critical path, limiting Fmax improvement to 4.37% with unchanged CoreMark cycles.

title: Move division out of the combinational EX path
motivation:
The baseline's measured worst path is 199.837 ns through forwarding and
u_ex/u_alu, with 156 cells, and median Fmax is only 5.442 MHz. The ALU
currently implements signed and unsigned division and remainder with
combinational / and % operators. These feed the shared EX result mux,
so their delay constrains every instruction, even when CoreMark executes
ordinary integer operations. There are no recorded structural attempts
or LESSONS.md entries for this core.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU hardware with one shared
blocking divider integrated into EX. Use a registered unsigned restoring
quotient/remainder datapath with four fixed restoring steps per clock:
eight iteration clocks replace the 32-step combinational division chain.
Normalize signed operands and execute the first four-bit chunk on the
launch edge, then execute the remaining seven chunks on subsequent edges.
Latch the forwarded operands and operation, and correct quotient/remainder
signs from registered results without adding a correction state.
Preserve division by zero and INT_MIN/-1 semantics exactly. MUL variants
and ordinary ALU operations retain their existing single-cycle behavior.

Add explicit launch, busy, result-valid and consume handshakes. Launch
only for a valid divide/remainder in EX when downstream backpressure
permits it. Hold PC and ID/EX until the result can enter EX/MEM. Older
EX/MEM and MEM/WB instructions must drain once; emit invalid EX/MEM
bubbles during division rather than repeatedly holding a retiring or
memory-accessing instruction. A genuine dmem stall instead holds its
pending EX/MEM request. Retain a completed divider result until accepted,
and never restart the held instruction. Latch the forwarded rs1/rs2 values
at launch so changing bypass sources during the wait cannot corrupt the
result or RVFI operands. Reset cancels all divider state.

Keep RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas identical to the existing contract,
with the same bounded divider handshake and iteration latency as real
hardware. The first chunk must count toward the eight iteration clocks;
do not add separate setup or correction clocks. Consume the completed
result into EX/MEM on the next edge when downstream is ready. This keeps
even a taken branch followed by division within the unchanged ten-clock
successor-retirement window under the formal wrapper's ready-high buses.
Do not change formal depths, assumptions, or liveness checks.
Retain the nret=1 interface, exact-once in-order retirement and memory
requests, trap discipline, and the existing memory-ready contract.
The expected Fmax gain from removing the deep divider should outweigh
the extra cycles spent on division. Accept only a measured fitness gain
above 4.6%; evaluate median Gowin Fmax times marker-bracketed CoreMark
iterations/cycle, including random imem and dmem stalls.

title: Small tagged next-PC predictor with two-bit branch hysteresis
motivation:
This core has no branch prediction: every taken conditional branch and every
JAL/JALR redirects from EX and discards the current fetch, even after a loop
or call site has executed many times. Its IF/ID bundle is combinational, so
the actual penalty is one younger instruction slot per redirect, rather
than the two-cycle penalty suggested by the five-stage comments. CoreMark's
repeated loops and call sites can recover these slots with a small learned
next-PC predictor. The measured critical path is through forwarding and
the combinational M-extension ALU; a shallow predictor lookup is expected
to improve iterations/cycle without extending that arithmetic path.

A reference-ISS profile of the canonical 2K, -O3, ten-iteration CoreMark
run, bounded by its start/stop MMIO stores, counted 2,922,016 instructions,
529,588 conditional branches, 49,367 JALs, and 13,735 JALRs. The baseline
incurs 357,527 taken-control redirects. An architectural trace model of
this 32-entry predictor produced 73,619 next-PC misses, saving 283,908
instruction slots; against the recorded 4,491,485 stalled baseline cycles
that corresponds to approximately 6.75% throughput gain at constant Fmax.
A 64-entry table improved that estimate only to 7.03%, making 32 entries
the stronger area/timing tradeoff. This is a trace estimate, with immediate
predictor updates and without replaying pipeline stalls; it is not an RTL
simulation or a measured FPGA improvement. The reference run matched all
five canonical CRCs and the required UART validation text.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 32-entry, direct-mapped, fully tagged branch-target buffer with
per-entry two-bit saturating conditional-branch direction counters. Index
with fetch PC[6:2], compare PC[31:7], and store aligned target[31:2], valid,
an unconditional-control-flow bit, and the counter. A miss predicts PC+4;
a tagged hit predicts the stored target for JAL/JALR or a conditional
counter with its high bit set. Allocate legal, aligned control transfers
when they advance through EX; initialize new conditional entries weakly
toward the observed outcome and update matching entries with saturation.
Refresh the resolved target for each accepted JALR. Use a modest table and
asynchronous lookup, reset only valid bits, and leave tag/target/counter
payload unreset to allow compact FPGA storage inference.

Carry the exact predicted next PC alongside each accepted instruction
through IF and ID/EX. Advance the fetch PC to this prediction only when
that instruction is actually admitted to ID/EX. In EX compute the same
architectural next PC as today, including sequential PC+4 on the existing
misalignment/trap path, and redirect only when it differs from the carried
prediction. Compare for every valid instruction, including nonbranches,
so a stale target entry cannot silently redirect a changed instruction.
Correct predictions must neither flush nor bubble the following fetch;
wrong direction and wrong target both recover to the resolved next PC.

Qualify resolution, correction, and predictor training with valid EX and
!stall_ex_mem, so a held instruction cannot redirect or train repeatedly.
Keep correction higher priority than an instruction-bus stall or a younger
load-use stall. During a data-bus stall hold fetch, ID/EX, and prediction
metadata; delay correction until EX can advance. Preserve MEM/WB operand
retention for forwarding. Suppress allocation for illegal or misaligned
transfers and invalidate a matching stale entry when EX resolves a
non-control instruction or a fault. Keep RVFI pc_wdata tied exclusively
to the resolved architectural next PC, and retain nret=1 and all existing
decode, arithmetic, memory, trap, and retirement-order checks.

Verify hot taken loops, a loop exit requiring predicted-taken recovery,
forward conditional branches, JAL, changing JALR targets, table collisions,
reset, and stale-entry recovery. Exercise instruction and data stalls at
prediction and correction, including a forwarded branch held behind a
stalled memory operation. Check retirement PCs, +1 RVFI order, and absence
of wrong-path stores. Run the existing unit tests, formal gate, and stalled
CoreMark cosim with canonical CRC/UART/timing-marker validation, then use
Gowin median Fmax times measured iterations/cycle for the fitness decision.

title: Segmented carry-select subtractors for the eight-edge divider
motivation:
The champion reaches 75.39 CoreMark iterations/second at 33.863 MHz,
but its reported worst path still ends at divider/remainder_q: 34.893 ns
and 109 cells from the register file through ID and EX. The divider
executes four dependent 33-bit subtract-and-restore steps per clock.
Each step's borrow selects the remainder before the next subtract can
finish. The earlier combinational radix-4 micro_opt gained only 4.37%
despite substantial area savings, showing that parallel quotient trials
and selection routing alone do not solve this bottleneck. Target the
carry propagation inside the successful registered restoring engine.

but its reported worst path still ends at divider/remainder_q: 34.893 ns
and 109 cells from the register file through ID and EX. The divider
executes four dependent 33-bit subtract-and-restore steps per clock.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace each of the existing four 33-bit restoring trial subtractors
with an explicitly segmented carry-select subtractor. Keep the restoring
algorithm, four quotient bits per edge, first chunk on launch, eight
iteration edges, and sticky result-valid/consume protocol unchanged.
This is a local combinational arithmetic optimization; do not add stages,
alter pipeline backpressure, or change the divider's completion latency.

Partition the low 32 bits into four 8-bit blocks. For each block j,
independently compute the 9-bit unsigned differences Xj-Dj and Xj-Dj-1,
representing incoming borrow zero and one. All operands must be explicitly
zero-extended before subtraction. Define block borrow-generate Gj as
bit 8 of Xj-Dj and borrow-propagate Pj as Xj==Dj. With B0=0, compute
every incoming block borrow directly with a balanced prefix network:
B1=G0; B2=G1|(P1&G0); B3=G2|(P2&G1)|(P2&P1&G0);
B4=G3|(P3&G2)|(P3&P2&G1)|(P3&P2&P1&G0).
Select each block's low eight difference bits using Bj. The divisor's
bit 32 is zero, so difference[32]=X[32]^B4 exactly reproduces the original
33-bit modular subtraction, including its sign/underflow decision.
Retain the existing choice between shifted remainder and difference
using difference[32], and the existing quotient-bit construction.
Avoid a serial four-block borrow recurrence or a fresh full-width
subtract in parallel with the segmented network; either would defeat
the intended shortening of the timing path.

The full-width carry chain becomes parallel short native carry chains,
a small borrow-prefix network, and block muxes. Apply this same helper
at all four restoring steps so both launch and busy feedback paths
benefit. Keep signed magnitude normalization and final sign correction
as they are. Preserve divide-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, unsigned high-bit
operands, and signed remainder semantics. Preserve the ALTOPS formulas
and their existing eight-edge handshake exactly. Keep nret=1, all traps,
in-order retirement, memory side effects, and bus-ready handling intact.

Validate subtraction against an independent 33-bit arithmetic reference,
especially borrow propagation through equal blocks and across bit 31.
Run the existing ALU and pipeline tests, formal ALTOPS gate, and cosim;
extend actual DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU vectors around byte boundaries and use
seeded random signed and unsigned operands. ALTOPS alone cannot validate
the real arithmetic. Measure median Gowin Fmax times canonical stalled,
marker-bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle. Marked cycles should remain
identical to the champion's 4,491,485 for ten iterations. The expected
gain is from Fmax, with some additional LUTs and routing as the main risk;
acceptance still requires more than 4.6% measured fitness improvement.

A standalone bit-accurate model of the specified block arithmetic passed
101,682 comparisons against independent 33-bit subtraction and 43,364
RV32M quotient/remainder comparisons against independent integer
arithmetic. These include directed block boundaries, both values of the
shifted remainder's top bit, random operands, zero divisors, and signed
overflow. This verifies the proposed equations, not implementing RTL
or FPGA timing; the predicted fitness gain remains unmeasured.

title: Retimed radix-4 divider with a narrow launch datapath
motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure only the existing blocking divider into separate launch and
iteration datapaths, retaining exactly eight arithmetic edges and the
existing launch/busy/result-valid/consume interface. On launch, normalize
and latch signed operands and sign metadata, compute the first four
quotient bits using a small prefix datapath, and register the divisor
multiples D and 3D at 34 bits; obtain 2D by shifting registered D. The
first dividend prefix is only four bits. Its four restoring decisions
can use widths 1, 2, 3 and 4, with mandatory high-divisor guards before
accepting each truncated subtraction. Do not route this launch prefix
through the generic full-width iteration network.

Each of the seven subsequent busy edges processes four more dividend
bits through two radix-4 digit stages instead of four serial radix-2
stages. For each stage form the 34-bit unsigned T=4*R+next_two_bits.
Compute T-D, T-2D and T-3D in parallel using 35-bit extended subtraction;
the high difference bit supplies the underflow predicate. Select the
largest fitting multiple with a small encoder and balanced remainder
mux, append its two-bit quotient digit, and feed the selected remainder
into the second stage. The iteration datapath reads registered state
and registered multiples only: no live forwarded operands, signed
normalization, launch-versus-busy operand mux, or multiples-generation
adder may precede its two-stage arithmetic recurrence. Unsigned R<D
bounds each selected remainder to 32 bits. Keep enough width for T and
all multiples, including divisors near UINT_MAX; truncating them is
incorrect. For D=0, generate all-one quotient digits and preserve the
dividend prefix as remainder, with quotient sign correction disabled.

The structural claim is that isolating the narrow launch computation
and halving serial full-width digit decisions shortens both candidate
divider timing paths without changing pipeline stalls or CoreMark IPC.
Registering 3D may move the bottleneck to its normalization-plus-add
path, and parallel trial subtracts cost area and routing; these are the
principal risks to the predicted gain. Preserve sticky result validity,
reset cancellation, result consumption, forwarded operand capture,
exact-once in-order retirement, and all existing bus-stall priorities.
Keep signed truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder,
division-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results correct. Retain the existing
ALTOPS formulas and the same eight-edge handshake in formal builds.
Add no setup or correction cycles, and preserve the ten-clock
branch-to-divide successor-retirement bound under ready-high buses.
Keep nret=1, all top-level ports, decoder/trap checks and eval files.

Validate actual arithmetic and unchanged latency with the existing ALU
and pipeline tests, directed digit-boundary and high-divisor cases,
formal, and canonical stalled CoreMark cosim. Judge the result by median

title: Direction-only branch prediction with decoded direct targets
motivation:
The champion already removes combinational division from the critical
path and reaches 33.863 MHz, but fetch still assumes PC+4 and loses one
younger instruction slot on every taken branch or jump. The IF/ID bundle
is combinational, so the real correction penalty is one slot, not the
two slots suggested by the five-stage comments. The earlier predictor
attempt reduced CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,208,674, demonstrating
useful branch locality, but its approximately 5.6 MHz divider-dominated
implementation did not retain the champion's eight-edge divider.
Use the current champion RTL as the base. A direction-only table can
exploit that locality without storing or selecting wide tagged targets.

A fresh reference-ISS profile of the canonical ten-iteration, 2K, -O3
CoreMark run counted 2,922,016 instructions inside the MMIO markers,
including 529,588 conditional branches, 49,367 JALs, and 13,735 JALRs.
Sequential prediction misses 357,527 next PCs. A 64-entry direction
table plus decoded JAL targets missed 65,592, including unpredicted
JALRs, saving an estimated 291,935 correction slots. Against the
champion's 4,491,485 cycles, this estimates 6.95% higher throughput
at constant Fmax. This model updates counters immediately, omits
pipeline/stall replay, and is not an RTL or FPGA measurement. The
reference execution matched every canonical CRC and validation text.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact, PC-indexed bimodal predictor with 64 two-bit saturating
direction counters. Read with fetch PC[7:2] and train with the resolving
branch's own PC[7:2]. Reset a per-entry initialized bitmap and interpret
uninitialized entries as weakly not taken; leave the counter payload
unreset for compact distributed-memory inference, and initialize it
from that default on the first accepted update. Predict only
legal conditional BRANCH encodings with funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7}; obtain
their target from the current instruction's B immediate plus fetch PC.
Predict legal JAL instructions unconditionally using their J immediate
plus fetch PC. JALR remains sequentially predicted and resolves in EX.
Suppress taken predictions for targets misaligned to four bytes. There
is no BTB, stored target, tag comparison, return stack, or global history:
counter aliases affect accuracy but cannot change instruction legality.
Implement compact storage and a shallow lookup; avoid synthesizing a
wide bank of target multiplexers or adding a pipeline stage.

Carry the exact predicted next PC with each instruction through IF and
ID/EX. It must be the value used to advance fetch for that accepted
instruction, not a later lookup of a potentially updated counter.
Fetch advances to that prediction only when ID/EX admits the instruction.
Existing load-use, imem, dmem, and divider waits hold PC and metadata.
EX computes the existing architectural next PC, including PC+4 for the
existing misalignment/trap path. Compare this resolved next PC against
the carried prediction, and flush only on a mismatch. Correctly predicted
branches and JALs must admit the younger instruction without a bubble;
both taken-to-sequential and sequential-to-taken corrections must work.
Keep RVFI pc_wdata tied to the resolved architectural next PC.

Gate correction and counter training with one accepted EX advancement:
in.valid && !reset && !stall_ex_mem && !divider_wait. Train only legal,
nonfaulting conditional branches, incrementing on taken and decrementing
on not taken with saturation. A held branch must not train or correct
repeatedly. Compare next PCs for every valid advancing instruction,
including JALR and trapped instructions. Keep accepted correction above
imem stalls and younger load-use holds; suppress it while an older dmem
request prevents EX advancement. Preserve all existing divider launch,
consume, operand capture, drain, and sticky-result behavior, including
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS. Preserve retained MEM/WB forwarding during stalls.

Retain the nret=1 ports, decoder legality rules, alignment traps,
in-order exact-once retirement, and exact-once memory side effects.
Keep every existing assertion and formal depth. Extend pipeline tests
for counter warmup, saturation, loop exits, forward branches, consecutive
predicted branches, direct JAL, JALR recovery, aliased PCs, reserved branch
encodings, misaligned targets, and reset. Combine load-use, divider, and
randomized bus stalls with prediction and recovery; verify RVFI PC chains,
monotonic order, operands, and absence of wrong-path stores. Run unchanged
correctness gates and marker-bracketed stalled CoreMark with all canonical
CRCs and UART validation. Score median Gowin Fmax times iterations/cycle;
the expected throughput gain must survive timing and exceed 4.6% overall.

title: Parallel one-hot forwarding and ALU operand selection
motivation:
The champion scores 98.03 at 44.029 MHz with 4,491,485 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its worst path begins at the register file and crosses operand
routing, branch resolution, IF and hazard logic back to ID. Divider
launch is another long live-operand path. The earlier shared combinational
divider gained only 4.37%, and segmented carry-select subtraction lost
22.46%, showing that arithmetic rewrites can add costly selection and
routing. Shorten the operand muxes common to branch and divider paths.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 98.03 at 44.029 MHz with 4,491,485 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its worst path begins at the register file and crosses operand
routing, branch resolution, IF and hazard logic back to ID. Divider
launch is another long live-operand path. The earlier shared combinational
divider gained only 4.37%, and segmented carry-select subtraction lost
22.46%, showing that arithmetic rewrites can add costly selection and
routing. Shorten the operand muxes common to branch and divider paths.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace encoded forwarding selects and cascaded data muxes with
mutually exclusive one-hot source enables and parallel masked-OR
operand selection. This is one local combinational mux optimization;
keep pipeline registers, divider latency, prediction, and bus handling.

For each EX source, compute M = EX/MEM valid writer, nonzero destination,
and matching source register; W = MEM/WB ctrl.reg_write, nonzero destination,
and matching source register. Emit three exclusive source enables:
ID = !M && !W, EXMEM = M, MEMWB = !M && W. Preserve EX/MEM priority and
x0 behavior exactly. Preserve MEM/WB forwarding without valid qualification:
its retained payload is required while dmem holds a dependent instruction.
Carry these three enables directly into EX rather than encoding them
into two bits and decoding them again. Use [0]=ID, [1]=EXMEM and
[2]=MEMWB, i.e. fwd_rs = {!M && W, M, !M && !W}. W must retain the
existing eligibility from ctrl.reg_write even when MEM/WB valid is clear.

Select architectural rs1 and rs2 with parallel masked ORs over ID/EX,
EX/MEM, and MEM/WB data. For the ALU operands, qualify those source enables
with !is_auipc or !alu_src and add the mutually exclusive PC or immediate
source. Specifically form a_sel = {is_auipc, fwd_rs1 & {3{!is_auipc}}}
and b_sel = {alu_src, fwd_rs2 & {3{!alu_src}}}. Construct ALU operands
as ORs of four data words ANDed with their replicated source enable;
[3] selects PC for A and immediate for B. Construct architectural rs1
and rs2 as the analogous three-source masked ORs using unqualified
forwarding enables. Select all four ALU candidates in parallel rather
than first constructing the forwarded operand and then applying a second
32-bit PC/immediate mux. Branch comparisons, JALR and store data must
continue to use architectural forwarded rs1/rs2, while AUIPC and immediate
ALU operations use the qualified ALU masks. Divider operand capture for
RVFI must still report architectural sources, never substituted PC/imm.

The expected benefit is less serial select/decode and wide data-mux logic
before branch resolution, ordinary ALU operations, and signed divider
launch normalization. Routing and enable fanout may outweigh the shorter
logic, or another path may become limiting. A temporary implementation
of this exact mux rewrite produced a 5.18%
median Fmax gain and unchanged marked CoreMark cycles, just above the
4.6% acceptance threshold. Do not carry forward the unsuccessful
invalid-payload probe. Avoid unrelated changes that could erase this
measured margin.

Preserve every existing reset, stall, flush, redirect, load-use, trap,
forwarding and retirement priority, the eight-edge divider and ALTOPS
expressions, and the nret=1 interface. Validate with the existing pipeline
and ALU suites, formal and full-trace selftest cosim under both ready-high
and stalled buses. Add focused cases where EX/MEM and MEM/WB both match a
source, different sources need different forwarding ages, x0 is targeted,
store/branch/JALR consume forwarded values, and a dependent instruction
needs held MEM/WB data during dmem backpressure. Check all RVFI sources,
results, contiguous orders and exact-once memory effects. Require canonical
CoreMark CRCs, UART validation, unchanged marked cycles and median Gowin
Fmax from all three placement options.

The isolated prototype was checked with the actual evaluator's Gowin flow
and unchanged single-retire timed wrapper and stall generator. A fresh
champion rebuild reproduced placement Fmax values 43.259, 44.029 and
44.029 MHz. The parallel-mux prototype produced 46.901, 46.308 and
46.308 MHz, median 46.308 MHz (+5.18%). Logic cells increased from 2,908
to 2,945; registers stayed at 597, with unchanged LUT-RAM, BSRAM and DSP
counts. The option-0 worst arrival fell from 28.411 to 26.616 ns and
now ends at divider launch rather than returning through IF/hazard/ID.

All 18 existing pipeline cocotb cases passed. Full retirement-trace cosim
passed selftest and all three random programs both with ready-high buses
and with random instruction/data stalls, eight checks total. Canonical
stalled CoreMark passed all five CRCs, the required UART validation
literal, bounded-access and termination checks. Its markers remained
15,801 and 4,507,286, exactly 4,491,485 measured cycles for ten iterations.
Prototype fitness is 103.10 iterations/second versus the champion's
98.03. These are measurements of a temporary candidate implementation;
the orchestrator must still implement this proposal and run every gate.
The prototype changed only forward_unit.sv, ex_stage.sv and core.sv.

An isolated copy of the unchanged single-retire formal wrapper and
checks_si.cfg passed all 53 ALTOPS formal checks with zero failures.
This verifies operand routing and pipeline behavior; actual arithmetic
was exercised by the pipeline and retirement-trace simulations above.

title: Decouple execute operand capture from squash and RAM outputs
motivation:
The champion reaches 44.029 MHz and 98.03 fitness at 4,491,485 marked
CoreMark cycles after the divider launch/iteration split. Its worst
path starts in register-file storage, traverses ID, EX, IF and hazard
logic, and returns to ID/EX operand storage. Vendor-timed isolated probes
expose two coupled limits at this same boundary: removing instruction
squash muxes alone leaves a BSRAM-output-to-divider path at 43.961 MHz;
an explicit flip-flop register file alone leaves EX redirect feeding
fetch masking and register reads at 44.954 MHz. Neither single-placement
result justifies acceptance. The promising structural hypothesis is one
independent operand-capture boundary, with explicit storage and validity
control that prevents both RAM absorption and squash feedback.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 44.029 MHz and 98.03 fitness at 4,491,485 marked
CoreMark cycles after the divider launch/iteration split. Its worst
path starts in register-file storage, traverses ID, EX, IF and hazard
logic, and returns to ID/EX operand storage. Vendor-timed isolated probes
expose two coupled limits at this same boundary: removing instruction
squash muxes alone leaves a BSRAM-output-to-divider path at 43.961 MHz;
an explicit flip-flop register file alone leaves EX redirect feeding
fetch masking and register reads at 44.954 MHz. Neither single-placement
result justifies acceptance. The promising structural hypothesis is one
independent operand-capture boundary, with explicit storage and validity
control that prevents both RAM absorption and squash feedback.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the existing fetch/decode-to-execute operand boundary so
wide instruction/operand payload is stored independently of instruction
validity, and integer register reads terminate in actual ID/EX operand
flip-flops. These are complementary requirements of the same boundary:
the array-style RF permits Gowin BSRAM read-output absorption, while
redirect-to-NOP masking feeds branch resolution back into read addresses
and wide ID/EX update logic. Preserve stage count, the single-issue
pipeline, sequential branch policy, and the current eight-edge divider.

Replace the RF array with 31 individually generated 32-bit flip-flop
words, each having its own synchronous reset and decoded write enable;
x0 is constant zero. Organize the read network as four groups of eight
register numbers. For each of two independent ports, share a five-bit
one-hot address decoder, mask words with their selects, reduce each
eight-word group with balanced OR logic, then combine the four groups.
Use fixed-index wiring rather than dynamic array accesses, so storage
cannot be inferred as RAM. Both ports must read arbitrary register pairs
without bank conflicts. Preserve write-first bypass on both ports and
x0 priority. Do not add registers inside reg_file or change port latency.

Expose raw imem_data and PC to decode, RF addresses and load-use matching
without the current redirect/flush NOP mux. Fetch validity is imemReady,
independent of redirect. Set hold = dmem_stall || divider_wait and
kill = load_use || accepted_redirect. On every nonheld edge, capture the
raw decoded payload and operands into ID/EX, regardless of kill or fetch
readiness; separately set valid = fetch_valid && !kill. Reset initializes
payload and clears valid. A true hold retains both. Load-use holds PC,
lets the load advance, and creates exactly one invalid EX slot; admit
the still-fetched dependent on the next available edge. Redirect kills
the younger slot and updates PC with existing priority over imem stalls.
An older unaccepted memory request holds ID/EX and suppresses EX
advancement and redirect. Preserve divider waits, older-stage draining,
operand capture, sticky results and consumption exactly as today.

Redirect/kill must not control IF instruction-data muxes, source read
addresses, hazard comparison operands, or wide ID/EX payload reset,
enable or data muxes. Only instruction validity and the fetch PC see
squash; do not remask raw decoded fields later and recreate the path.
Keep conservative load-use source matching, rather than adding a source
usage optimization. Keep existing EX/MEM divider bubbles and the rest
of the pipeline topology. Verify the vendor netlist has explicit RF
word and ID/EX operand flip-flops, with no register-file BSRAM instances.

Audit all effect and hazard enables against their stage's valid bit.
Arbitrary invalid payloads must not launch division, redirect, issue
memory requests, write registers, create dependencies or retire. The
existing MEM/WB bypass deliberately survives WB.valid clearing on a
memory stall: preserve that retained result/destination behavior. On a
normal MEM/WB capture, qualify its stored reg_write/bypass eligibility
with EX/MEM.valid and existing trap suppression, so an invalid writing
opcode cannot become a false bypass. During hold_wb, retain data, tag
and eligibility and clear only retirement valid, exactly as before.
Do not simply gate MEM/WB bypass by retirement valid.

This spends about 992 RF storage flip-flops plus read-selection LUTs to
remove both measured operand-delivery limits without extra instruction
cycles. High-fanout decode/write nets, placement congestion and the
registered divider recurrence are the principal remaining timing risks.
Keep nret=1, every core port, decoder default-illegal rules, alignment
traps, RV32M arithmetic and ALTOPS formulas, contiguous in-order RVFI
retirement, exact-once memory effects, and the ready-high ten-clock
branch-to-divide successor bound. Change no eval or formal contracts.

Run unchanged unit tests, formal and canonical stalled CoreMark; extend
RF all-address/same-group/bypass/reset tests and adversarial invalid
payload tests. Cover killed loads, stores, divides, jumps, illegal
instructions and writes aliasing live operands, along with load-use
replay and retained WB bypass during prolonged memory stalls. Check
all canonical CRCs and validation text, compare marker-bracketed cycles
to 4,491,485, and inspect timing for elimination of both RF BSRAM launches
and redirect-to-read-address feedback. Accept only median vendor Gowin
Fmax times iterations/cycle more than 4.6% above 98.03. Prototype
measurements do not replace the full formal and evaluator gates.

A temporary RTL prototype of this complete operand-boundary change
passed all 18 existing pipeline tests, all five RF unit tests, and
320 additional seeded sequences checking killed side effects and
invalid load-use payloads. The unchanged CoreMark harness with both
random bus stalls completed in exactly 4,491,485 marked cycles, without
out-of-bounds accesses, with all canonical CRCs and validation text.
Vendor builds for placement options 0/1/2 returned 48.521/47.279/47.279
MHz, giving 47.279 MHz median and implied fitness 105.26, or +7.38%
against 98.03. Option 0 used 4,100 logic cells, 1,538 registers, four
BSRAMs and six DSPs; the RF BSRAM/read-output path and IF squash chain
disappeared from its worst paths. Its new worst path is 25.904 ns
through forwarding and divider launch. These are probe results on a

title: Bimodal direct prediction with one-bit EX recovery
motivation:
The current champion reaches 98.03 iterations/second at 44.029 MHz,
but still fetches sequentially and discards one younger instruction
slot for each taken branch or jump. The previous 64-entry direction
predictor reduced marker-bracketed stalled CoreMark cycles from
4,491,485 to 4,201,740, a 6.90% throughput opportunity, but was evaluated
on the older divider and reached only 36.810 MHz. Start from the current
champion, including its retimed radix-4 divider. Its reported worst path
now crosses EX branch recovery, IF instruction masking, the hazard unit,
and the ID register. Predictor accuracy must therefore be obtained with
shallow recovery logic, rather than a wide next-PC comparison or a
redirect-dependent instruction mux feeding hazard/decode logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 64-entry PC-indexed bimodal direction predictor for legal
conditional branches, with two-bit saturating counters and a weakly
not-taken cold state. Index by PC[7:2], reset only an initialized bitmap,
and leave counter payload unreset. On a cold update saturate from the
virtual cold state. Train exactly once when a legal, nonfaulting branch
advances through EX. Use the currently fetched instruction to recognize
legal BRANCH funct3 values {0,1,4,5,6,7} and JAL; predict JAL taken and
JALR sequential. Compute direct targets from the instruction's B/J
immediate and fetch PC, preferably as an aligned 30-bit word-address
addition. Predict taken only for four-byte-aligned direct targets.
This is one direct-control prediction mechanism, with no stored-target
BTB, global history, return stack, or extra pipeline stage.

Carry only a predicted_taken bit in IF and ID/EX, captured atomically
with each admitted instruction. For legal aligned direct branches and
JAL, the fetch target and EX target come from the same instruction and
PC, so correction requires no 32-bit predicted-next-PC register or
equality comparison. For a conditional branch, recover when the bit
differs from the effective resolved direction: actual branch_taken
qualified by !misalign_fault. A predicted-taken branch resolving not
taken recovers to PC+4; a predicted-not-taken branch resolving taken
recovers to its direct target. Aligned JAL is correctly predicted;
JALR retains ordinary EX target recovery. For misaligned direct jumps,
suppress prediction and retain the existing trap/sequential behavior.
Keep RVFI pc_wdata driven by the architectural resolved next PC.

Qualify correction and training with valid EX advancement, !reset,
!stall_ex_mem, and !divider_wait. Correct prediction admits the younger
instruction without a flush. Accepted correction overrides imem waits
and younger load-use holds, while older dmem stalls defer resolution.
Hold fetch PC and its metadata on load-use, bus, and divider waits.
Do not let EX correction select a NOP on the combinational IF instr
path: retain the fetched instruction for predecode and hazards, and
kill the younger instruction directly with ID/EX flush. Derive hazard
source comparisons from that raw instruction and qualify with bus
validity; route correction directly to ID/EX flush and PC priority.
A wrong-path load-use match must not prevent correction or fetching
its target. This removes the existing EX-to-IF-instruction-mux-to-hazard
dependency from recovery without adding correction latency.

Preserve the champion divider's launch/consume, operand capture,
eight-edge latency, drain, and sticky-result behavior, and preserve
retained MEM/WB forwarding during dmem stalls. Keep the nret=1 port
contract, decoder default-illegal behavior, alignment traps, exact-once
memory effects, and in-order RVFI retirement. Extend existing pipeline
tests for warmup/saturation, loop exits, forward branches, consecutive
predictions, JAL, JALR, aliases, reserved encodings, misaligned targets,
and reset. Exercise prediction and correction with load-use/divider
waits and randomized instruction/data backpressure; check RVFI PC
chains, operands, +1 order, and absence of wrong-path stores. Run the
unchanged correctness gates and canonical stalled CoreMark validation,
then evaluate median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle.
With the previous measured cycle reduction, exceeding the 4.6%
acceptance threshold requires retaining roughly 43.1 MHz or better;
preserve timing by using one-bit recovery and a compact direction table.

title: Boolean nibble lookup for the divider launch prefix
motivation:
The champion scores 107.88 at 48.454 MHz with 4,491,485 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its worst vendor path starts at MEM/WB destination matching,
crosses forwarding, and ends at divider/quotient_q bit zero. The launch
cone still normalizes signed operands, reduces the full divisor for
high-bit guards, and serially executes four restoring decisions. Prior
micro_opt attempts show that full-width carry-select subtractors hurt
timing and that forwarding cleanup alone does not beat the champion.
Optimize the bounded four-bit launch function itself rather than the
registered full-width recurrence.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 107.88 at 48.454 MHz with 4,491,485 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its worst vendor path starts at MEM/WB destination matching,
crosses forwarding, and ends at divider/quotient_q bit zero. The launch
cone still normalizes signed operands, reduces the full divisor for
high-bit guards, and serially executes four restoring decisions. Prior
micro_opt attempts show that full-width carry-select subtractors hurt
timing and that forwarding cleanup alone does not beat the champion.
Optimize the bounded four-bit launch function itself rather than the
registered full-width recurrence.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the divider's four serial launch-prefix restoring decisions
with one combinational four-bit quotient/remainder lookup. Keep the
existing eight-edge completion latency (launch plus seven busy edges),
two radix-4 digits per busy edge, registered divisor multiples, launch/
consume handshake and pipeline backpressure. This is a local launch
datapath optimization with no new state or instruction cycles.

Let P be the top nibble of the unsigned dividend magnitude and D the
unsigned divisor magnitude. For 1 <= D <= 15, emit Q=P/D and R=P%D
directly from a fully specified 16-by-16 combinational truth table
indexed by P and D[3:0]. The D=0 column must emit Q=15 and R=P, matching
the existing natural divide-by-zero recurrence. For D >= 16, emit Q=0
and R=P. Generate the table as minimized combinational Boolean equations,
not a case ROM, clocked lookup or inferred memory, and do not use
variable / or % operators in synthesizable RTL. Feed the unchanged
launch registers with quotient_q={magnitude_a[27:0],Q} and
remainder_q={28'b0,R}. The lookup replaces all four dependent narrow
subtract/select stages; do not retain a duplicate restoring network.

A deterministic implementation is eight independent sums of products
for the bits of {Q,R}, indexed by x={divisor_nibble,prefix_nibble}.
Generate minterms from the complete 256-entry table, merge cubes with
identical masks that differ in one specified bit until only prime
implicants remain, and select every essential prime. Greedily cover
uncovered minterms with the prime covering the most remaining ones;
break ties by fewer specified bits, then ascending (value,mask).
Emit selected cubes in ascending (value,mask) order as explicit bitwise
AND terms joined by OR. Bit zero of x is P[0], bit seven is D[3]. This
produces 21,22,17,8,27,10,4,2 product terms for R[0:3] then Q[0:3].
No ROM initializer, indexed constant array, dynamic table shift or
variable arithmetic divider is needed. Confirm the vendor netlist
retains four total BSRAMs, zero LUT-RAMs and 1,538 registers, matching
the champion; a flat case table was observed to infer an extra BSRAM
and underperform the Boolean implementation.

Avoid routing a full 32-bit signed-negation carry chain or normalized
divisor high-bit reduction into this bounded lookup. Define neg_a and
neg_b as signed_op && operand[31]. Obtain P directly: for neg_a use
(~a[31:28]) + (a[27:0] == 0), with explicit four-bit modular arithmetic;
otherwise use a[31:28]. The top nibble needs only a lower-bit zero
reduction and a four-bit carry, not all bits of -a. Obtain the low
divisor nibble as neg_b ? (4'b0-b[3:0]) : b[3:0]. The exact small-divisor
predicate is neg_b ? (&b[31:4] && (|b[3:0])) : !(|b[31:4]). For a negative
signed operand only -1 through -15 qualify; -16, INT_MIN, and unsigned
high-bit operands must use the D>=16 bypass. Zero qualifies through the
nonnegative arm and uses the explicitly defined zero column. Preserve
full magnitude_a/magnitude_b where they still initialize the low
dividend bits and registered D/3D; these signals must no longer feed
the launch quotient/remainder cone.

Preserve every RV32M bit result, including zero divisors, signed
truncation toward zero, the dividend sign for REM, and INT_MIN/-1.
Preserve ALTOPS formulas and their existing latency exactly. Preserve
nret=1, all top-level ports, decoder legality rules, alignment traps,
retirement order and exact-once memory effects. Retain all existing
tests and checks. Extend the local arithmetic proof to compare the
new prefix against the independent identity P=Q*D+R and R<D for D>0,
plus the zero-divisor identity, while keeping both recurrence proofs.
Exhaustively verify all 256 nibble pairs and signed prefix/carry
boundaries; exercise full DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU results with independent
references and held-result/back-to-back operation tests. Run the
existing unit tests, formal gate and canonical stalled CoreMark cosim.

Expect unchanged marked CoreMark cycles and a median Gowin Fmax gain
exceeding the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. Table mapping, guard
fanout, the retained D/3D preparation path and the registered recurrence
may limit the gain; vendor timing must verify this rather than assuming
a shallow lookup from its small truth table.

A temporary Boolean RTL prototype passed warning-free full-core lint,
all 30 existing ALU tests and all 21 existing pipeline tests. A local
Yosys SAT proof without ALTOPS proved direct top-nibble normalization,
exact small-divisor classification and low-nibble normalization for
arbitrary raw operands, the launch quotient/remainder identities and
both existing full-width recurrence invariants. The unchanged CoreMark
harness with random instruction/data stalls completed in exactly
4,491,485 marked cycles with all canonical CRCs and validation text,
valid timing brackets and no out-of-bounds accesses.

Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 51.960/54.059/54.059 MHz on this
prototype, yielding 54.059 MHz median and implied fitness 120.36, or
+11.57 percent versus the champion. Option zero used 4,184 logic cells,
1,538 registers, zero LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs. Its worst path
moved out of divider launch to the forwarding/ALU-to-memory path,
with 24.540 ns arrival and 13 cells. These are isolated prototype
measurements; the implementing agent must reproduce the change and
run every unchanged evaluator gate, including full pipeline formal.

title: Pipeline divider initialization without adding division latency
motivation:
The current champion scores 107.88 at 48.454 MHz and 4,491,485 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its measured worst path is 25.906 ns from the retained
MEM/WB destination through forwarding and EX into the divider quotient
register. Earlier structural changes removed combinational division,
shortened the registered recurrence, and isolated ID/EX operand storage;
forwarding plus signed normalization plus launch-prefix arithmetic is
now the remaining measured divider input bottleneck. Adding division
clocks would risk the unchanged ten-clock branch-to-divide formal bound.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current champion scores 107.88 at 48.454 MHz and 4,491,485 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its measured worst path is 25.906 ns from the retained
MEM/WB destination through forwarding and EX into the divider quotient
register. Earlier structural changes removed combinational division,
shortened the registered recurrence, and isolated ID/EX operand storage;
forwarding plus signed normalization plus launch-prefix arithmetic is
now the remaining measured divider input bottleneck. Adding division
clocks would risk the unchanged ten-clock branch-to-divide formal bound.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the blocking divider into a normalized-input register stage,
an exact small-prefix initialization stage, and its existing registered
recurrence, keeping exactly eight edges from accepted launch through
result_valid. This is a divider pipeline-boundary change, with no new
general pipeline stage or change to the instruction retirement width.

Edge 1 captures the forwarded operands as unsigned 32-bit magnitudes
and captures quotient/remainder sign and operation metadata. Do not
compute quotient digits or 3D on this edge. Thus the live forwarding
path ends after signed normalization, instead of continuing into prefix
subtract/select logic or a full-width multiples adder. Preserve the EX
capture of original forwarded operands for RVFI. Reuse quotient_q for
the captured magnitude A, divisor_q for zero-extended magnitude B, and
initialize remainder_q to zero. Add one real-datapath prefix-phase bit
instead of duplicating the 64-bit normalized operand storage.

Edge 2 reads only those registered magnitudes, processes the first eight
dividend bits, and registers the initial quotient/remainder and 34-bit
D and 3D. Compute the first four-bit quotient/remainder directly with
a complete 256-entry constant case table indexed by the four-bit
dividend prefix and D[3:0]. Every entry is generated from independent
integer quotient/remainder arithmetic; for a zero divisor encode Q=15
and R=the prefix. When D[31:4] is nonzero, override the table with Q=0
and R=the prefix, because a four-bit dividend is smaller than D. This
is a fixed four-bit arithmetic truth table, independent of fetched
code, addresses, workload, or benchmark data. Let Gowin implement its
exact combinational function rather than serializing four decisions.
Append the next four dividend bits with just two tapered radix-4 digit
decisions at widths 6 and 8. Compute parallel T-D, T-2D and T-3D,
derive fits from extended subtraction borrow plus all omitted-multiple
bits being zero, then use the existing balanced digit/remainder select.
Keep prefix multiples narrow: when D[31:8] is nonzero, no multiple fits
any eight-bit prefix, so emit zero prefix digits and retain A[31:24].
Otherwise use zero-extended D[7:0], 9-bit 2D and 10-bit 3D, retaining
their high-bit guards at every tapered width. The full 34-bit 3D adder
runs in parallel to prefix arithmetic and feeds its own register; it
must not feed the prefix decision chain. For D=0, all candidates fit,
yielding eight all-one quotient bits and the dividend prefix remainder.
Initialize Q={magnitude_a[23:0], prefix_quotient[7:0]} and zero-extend
the eight-bit prefix remainder to 32 bits.

Edges 3 through 8 each process four more dividend bits with the existing
two full-width radix-4 digit stages fed exclusively by registered Q,
R, D and 3D. The schedule consumes 8+6*4=32 dividend bits. Assert sticky
result_valid on edge 8 and allow the existing next-edge EX/MEM consume;
add neither a setup clock nor a sign-correction clock to visible latency.
Distinguish the prefix phase from the six recurrence phases explicitly.
Keep signed sign-correction on the completed registered result, signed
truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, divide-by-zero, and
INT_MIN/-1 semantics. Suppress quotient negation for a zero divisor.

Preserve launch/busy/result_valid/consume behavior, including rejection
of requests while busy and while an unconsumed result is pending,
same-edge consume/new-launch support, and reset cancellation in every
phase. Changing live ALU inputs after launch must affect neither prefix
initialization nor subsequent arithmetic. Keep the existing ALTOPS
formulas and identical eight-edge control schedule in formal builds.
Preserve EX drain bubbles, true dmem holds, retained WB forwarding,
exact-once side effects, contiguous in-order RVFI retirement, nret=1,
all core ports, decoder legality and traps. Ordinary ALU operations and
multiplication keep their existing latency and topology.

Validate all current checks, especially the unchanged eight-edge ALU
handshake and ten-clock ready-high branch-to-divide bound. Extend the
local arithmetic proof to establish A[31:24]=prefix_Q*D+prefix_R with
prefix_R<D for D>0, the zero-divisor prefix identity, the exhaustive
four-bit table identity, both tapered digit identities, and the existing
full-width recurrence identities. Adapt internal per-edge prefix checks
to zero bits consumed after edge 1, then 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28 and 32;
retain exact per-phase remainder identities and all latency assertions.
Use independent real-arithmetic vectors at D=63/64, 85/86, 127/128,
255/256 and larger divisors, digit boundaries, all signs and overflow.
Check reset during initialization, busy relaunch attempts, held results,
operand changes, forwarding, chained divisions and randomized bus stalls.

The expected fitness improvement comes from higher Fmax with unchanged
CoreMark cycles. The table plus two narrow decisions, normalization alone,
and the unchanged full-width recurrence compete to become the new worst
path; prefix routing is the main risk. Run canonical stalled CoreMark
and median vendor Gowin timing. With unchanged cycles, acceptance above
107.88 requires more than approximately 50.683 MHz median Fmax. The
predicted improvement requires the full evaluator gates.

A temporary RTL prototype of this schedule with the exact four-bit
case table reaches 51.921 MHz in Gowin placement option 0, versus the
champion's 48.454 MHz median. Its worst path moves out of the divider
to forwarding/multiplication and the data-memory address, at 24.555 ns.
Placement options 0/1/2 return 51.921/53.138/53.138 MHz: median 53.138
MHz, a 9.67% frequency gain. The unchanged canonical stalled CoreMark
harness completes in exactly 4,491,485 marked cycles with canonical
CRCs and validation text, implying fitness 118.31 versus 107.88.
The prototype passes 30 ALU and 21 pipeline cocotb tests, including
exact arithmetic, busy-input mutation, eight-edge result timing and
the unchanged ten-clock branch-to-divide bound. Only the ALU test's
internal edge-1 prefix identity is adapted to zero bits consumed;
every later prefix identity and completion deadline is retained.
Selftest cosim passes both ready-high and random instruction/data
stalls. A local SAT proof passes the complete eight-bit prefix
identity and remainder bound, both narrow digit identities, and the
original full-width recurrence and zero-divisor identities. Its ROM
is mapped to gates before SAT; this is a proof-lowering step, not a
changed assertion or assumption. Vendor area is 4,172 logic cells,
1,553 registers, five BSRAMs and six DSPs, versus the champion's
4,155/1,538/four/six. The arithmetic case table accounts for the extra
BSRAM. These measurements are from temporary source copies; the full
unchanged riscv-formal gate and evaluator must still pass after
implementation. Timing and finite cosim do not replace those gates.

Adapt the existing local real-arithmetic invariant proof to the
registered eight-bit prefix and prove the exact four-bit table and
both tapered digit identities,
omitted-multiple guards, prefix quotient/remainder identity and
zero-divisor behavior. Retain the full-width recurrence checks and
the requirement that the proof succeed; map the inferred constant
ROM to gates before SAT so the proof supports the new arithmetic
table. Keep wrapper/formal contracts, depths and assumptions unchanged;
retain all recurrence assertions and strengthen the prefix checks.

Preserve all existing exact-result and eight-edge latency assertions.
Add directed eight-bit prefix/multiple boundaries and input mutation
between launch and initialization, reset in each new phase, rejected
launches, held completion and same-edge consume/new-launch cases.

Retain the ten-clock branch-to-divide bound and all existing checks.

title: Static backward-taken prediction with one-bit recovery
motivation:
The champion loses one younger instruction slot on every taken branch
or jump because its IF/ID interface is combinational and EX redirects
unconditionally. Previous dynamic predictors recovered about 6.9%
iterations/cycle but added direction storage, lookup, and update logic.
A fresh 64-entry prototype on the current squash-isolated champion
reproduced 4,201,740 CoreMark cycles but reached only 45.091 MHz median
Gowin Fmax, giving approximately 107.32 iterations/sec. Preserving the
clock rate matters more than the last fraction of prediction accuracy.

An isolated static backward-taken/forward-not-taken prototype instead
measured 4,259,699 marked cycles and placement Fmax values 45.386,
49.231, and 49.231 MHz with metadata above the existing packed fields:
approximately 115.57 iterations/sec, 7.13% above the 107.88 champion.
It passed canonical CoreMark CRCs,
required UART text, termination, and bounded-access checks under the
unchanged instruction/data stall methodology. These are prototype
measurements; the implementation and unchanged eval gates must still
confirm the result. All 21 existing pipeline tests, eight selftest/random
trace comparisons with and without bus stalls, and all 53 unchanged
ALTOPS formal checks passed. A fresh champion timing build reproduced
48.454 MHz. The static mechanism is the single proposed angle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a stateless backward-taken/forward-not-taken direct-control
predictor to the current champion. Predict a legal conditional branch
taken exactly when its signed B immediate is negative (instruction
bit 31); predict legal JAL taken; predict all other instructions,
including JALR, sequentially. Recognize BRANCH only for funct3 values
{0,1,4,5,6,7}. Suppress direct predictions for targets misaligned to
four bytes: with aligned fetch PC, B immediate bit 1 is instr[8] and
J immediate bit 1 is instr[21]. This exploits loop locality without
any table, counter, tag, target cache, training port, or history state.

Compute the predicted direct target from the raw fetched instruction
and fetch PC with a 30-bit word-address addition. For B instructions,
offset_word is {{20{instr[31]}},instr[7],instr[30:25],instr[11:9]}.
For JAL it is {{12{instr[31]}},instr[19:12],instr[20],instr[30:22]}.
Set target to {(pc[31:2] + offset_word),2'b00}, with addition truncated
to 30 bits for ordinary RV32 wraparound. Require aligned fetch PC and
check the omitted immediate bit 1 before enabling a prediction. Advance
fetch to this target only when the instruction is actually admitted
to ID/EX; otherwise preserve the existing PC holds.

Carry one predicted_taken bit in if_id_t and id_ex_t as the most
significant packed field, preserving every existing field's bit offset
and the existing unit tests' bundle layout expectations. Capture and hold
it with ordinary instruction payload; it records the prediction used
for that instruction, even when load-use, bus, or divider waits occur.
For legal aligned direct controls, IF and EX derive identical targets
from the same instruction and PC, so EX correction needs only a
direction-bit comparison, not stored predicted targets or wide next-PC
equality. Define direct_taken as !misalign_fault && !is_illegal &&
(branch_taken || (is_jump && !is_jalr)). An accepted instruction needs
correction when direct_taken differs from predicted_taken, or when
it is an aligned JALR requiring the existing EX target redirect.
Recover taken-to-not-taken misses to PC+4 and not-taken-to-taken misses
to the existing resolved branch/jump target. Correctly predicted
branches and JALs admit the younger fetch without a squash. Misaligned
transfers retain the existing trap, suppressed writeback, and sequential
next-PC behavior. RVFI pc_wdata remains the architectural resolved PC.

Qualify correction with valid EX advancement, !reset, !stall_ex_mem,
and !divider_wait. Accepted correction has priority over instruction-
bus waits and younger load-use holds; an older data-memory stall
defers resolution. Preserve the champion's raw instruction bus and
source addresses, explicit flip-flop register file, and separation
of reset/hold payload capture from validity-only kill. Prediction and
correction must not select replacement instructions, gate operand
capture, or change the RF or divider. Retain MEM/WB bypass eligibility
during data stalls and the eight-edge divider's launch/consume,
sticky result, drain, operand capture, and ALTOPS behavior.

Keep nret=1, every top-level port, decoder default-illegal discipline,
alignment traps, exact-once memory effects, in-order RVFI retirement,
and all existing checks. Validate backward taken loops and loop exits,
forward taken and not-taken branches, all six legal branch conditions,
positive/negative JAL offsets, JALR, consecutive predicted controls,
reserved branch encodings, misaligned B/J targets, reset, and PC
wraparound. Combine correction with instruction/data backpressure,
load-use stalls, forwarding, and divider waits. Check RVFI PC continuity,
operands/results, contiguous order, and absence of wrong-path stores.
Run unchanged formal and cosim gates and marker-bracketed canonical
CoreMark with all five CRCs and required validation text.

The measured cycle gain is 5.44%, slightly less than the dynamic table,
but the static prototype adds only 106 logic cells and two registers
in the timed wrapper (4,261 logic / 1,540 registers versus the recorded
4,155 / 1,538). At 4,259,699 cycles, clearing the 4.6% acceptance margin
requires approximately 48.07 MHz median Fmax. Verify all three Gowin
placement options; the prototype's 49.231 MHz median clears this margin,
while its lower option-0 result makes timing confirmation important.
The main risks are fetch-target adder routing and changed placement of
the unchanged forwarding-to-divider path, not predictor state accuracy.

title: Register bypass matches alongside ID/EX operand capture
motivation:
The champion scores 121.32 at 51.680 MHz with 4,259,699 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its 24.772 ns worst path starts at EX/MEM destination
metadata and crosses forwarding into the divider launch remainder.
Earlier micro_opt attempts shortened arithmetic or data muxes, but
forwarding comparisons still precede the divider and multiplier.
Register those small control predicates at the existing ID/EX boundary
to remove destination comparison from every EX operand timing path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming only the bypass-match predicates into four flip-flops removes
the live five-bit destination comparators from execute operand selection.
Capture one EX/MEM match and one MEM/WB match per source alongside the
existing ID/EX operand capture. Keep the instruction pipeline, register
file, encoded forwarding muxes, prediction, all arithmetic and divider
latency unchanged. This is a local forwarding-control micro-optimization;
no instruction stage or operand-data register is added.

On an edge that captures a new ID/EX slot, compare its raw IF/ID source
addresses against the current ID/EX and EX/MEM destinations. Current
ID/EX becomes next EX/MEM; current EX/MEM becomes next MEM/WB. Qualify
each match by the actual write eligibility of the producer after that
edge, and by rd!=0. Do not register matches against the old MEM/WB
destination: its write is already visible through the RF's same-cycle
write-first bypass during operand capture. Source addresses and raw
operand capture retain their current validity-only squash behavior.

Export next_EXMEM_bypass_eligible from EX as in.valid &&
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write && !divider_wait. It describes the writer
actually entering EX/MEM, including suppressed writes on misaligned
JAL/JALR. Export next_MEMWB_bypass_eligible from MEM as the existing
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write, which already includes in.valid and suppresses
writes on misaligned loads. Use these eligibility predicates only on
edges where their producer stages advance. For each newly captured
source s, assign M_s = next_EXMEM_bypass_eligible && id_ex.rd!=0 &&
id_ex.rd==s, and W_s = next_MEMWB_bypass_eligible && ex_mem.rd!=0 &&
ex_mem.rd==s. Both matches may be set; select EX/MEM over MEM/WB exactly
as the current forward_unit does, and otherwise select captured RF data.
Keep the existing 00/01/10 forwarding-select interface to EX.

Update metadata with the same reset/hold transitions as the actual
producer registers. Reset clears all four matches. A true dmem stall
holds ID/EX and EX/MEM and retains WB payload/eligibility while clearing
only WB.valid, so hold all matches unchanged. A divider wait without
a dmem stall holds the consumer in ID/EX but drains EX/MEM into WB and
inserts an invalid EX/MEM slot. On each such edge clear M_s and set
W_s to the old M_s && next_MEMWB_bypass_eligible. Subsequent drain
bubbles clear WB eligibility naturally. Holding metadata takes priority
over aging when an older memory request stalls. If ID captures a slot,
use the fresh comparisons described above. Merely holding metadata
whenever ID is held would be incorrect in the divide-drain case.

WB bypass remains eligible when retirement-valid has been cleared by
a dmem stall. The retained WB result and the real load/ALU WB data mux
remain unchanged. Preserve younger-EX/MEM writer priority, x0,
forwarded branch/JALR/store values, forwarded divide launch inputs,
and the divide's captured RVFI sources when older instructions drain.
Load-use replay and validity-only squash retain their current behavior.

Preserve nret=1, every core port, decoder default-illegal discipline,
alignment traps, correction/hold priority, eight-edge real and ALTOPS
divider schedules, in-order contiguous RVFI retirement, and exact-once
memory effects. Retain every existing test and correctness check.
Add cycle-by-cycle comparisons of the registered forwarding selections
against the original combinational destination-match equations, using
actual current pipeline state and retained WB eligibility. Exercise
all source ages, simultaneous matching writers, independent sources,
x0, loads and load-use bubbles, misaligned producer suppression, killed
younger instructions, divide launch/drain/consume, dmem holds before
and after divide completion, and reset. Check architectural RVFI
operands/results, order, PC continuity and memory side effects under
ready-high and randomized instruction/data bus backpressure.

Verify with unchanged pipeline and ALU tests, local divider arithmetic
proof, full single-retire formal gate and canonical stalled CoreMark
cosim. Expect exactly the champion's marked cycles, with improved
median Gowin Fmax from the shorter forwarding control path. Acceptance
above 121.32 requires roughly 54.06 MHz at those cycles. Data-driven
divider launch, multiplication, or match-register placement may limit
the gain; use all three vendor placement options. The timing gain is
an unmeasured prediction until the prototype/evaluator confirms it.

title: Register bypass decisions and the selected writeback value
motivation:
The champion reaches 51.680 MHz and 4,259,699 marked CoreMark cycles,
giving 121.32 iterations/sec. Its worst reported path starts at an
EX/MEM destination-tag register and crosses u_fwd and EX operand muxes
before reaching the divider launch remainder register: 24.772 ns and
21 cells. Earlier structural attempts removed register-file RAM-output
absorption and retimed divider initialization. The latter moved the
bottleneck to a WB destination-tag through forwarding/multiplication
path, so optimizing just the divider leaves another instance of the
same dependency-selection delay. No prior structural attempt registered
the bypass decisions. Moving tag matching across ID/EX and selecting
the authoritative writeback value before MEM/WB can shorten both
arithmetic paths without adding a stage or changing instruction cycles.

Isolated vendor probes expose both parts of this operand-delivery limit.
Registered bypass decisions alone reached 51.719 MHz median, with the
worst path moving to WB mem_to_reg selection through divider launch;
that partial change does not clear the acceptance margin. Completing
the same boundary change by registering the selected WB value reached
52.143, 56.328 and 56.328 MHz across placement options 0/1/2. Stalled
canonical CoreMark retained exactly 4,259,699 marked cycles, passed CRC,
UART, bounded-access and termination validation, and implies 132.23
iterations/sec, approximately 9.0 percent above the 121.32 champion.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retime the operand-delivery network at its existing ID/EX and MEM/WB
boundaries: register EX bypass decisions alongside ID/EX operands and
store an already-selected final writeback value in MEM/WB. This is one
structural change to where bypass control and result selection occur.
Move EX bypass dependency selection into decode and register the two
bypass selectors alongside the existing ID/EX operand payload. Keep
execution data forwarding from the registered EX/MEM and MEM/WB values;
only the source-tag comparison and priority decision move one cycle
earlier. Preserve stage count and all instruction latencies. At an
admitted decode edge, today's valid EX producer becomes tomorrow's
EX/MEM producer, and today's accepted MEM producer becomes tomorrow's
MEM/WB producer. Compare raw fetched rs1/rs2 addresses with those two
producers' destinations, select younger EX over older MEM over captured
RF data, exclude x0, and latch selectors on exactly the same reset/hold
edges as the existing ID/EX payload. EX then consumes registered
selectors directly instead of comparing registered producer tags in
the same combinational cone as normalization, divider prefix work,
multiplication, and branch comparison.

Use the producers' actual next-stage write eligibility, not unqualified
decoder reg_write bits. The younger producer must be valid and use the
EX control after branch/jump alignment-trap suppression; the older must
be valid and use MEM control after memory alignment-trap suppression.
Capture only when downstream hold is absent, which already guarantees
EX advancement and MEM acceptance. A load-use bubble must still prevent
admission of an immediate dependent on an EX load. On its replay edge,
that load is in MEM, so preselection correctly chooses the next WB load
result. Keep existing conservative load-use matching unchanged. Do not
build a combinational EX-result-to-ID operand bypass or register new
forwarded data: the data sources and arithmetic stay in EX.

In MEM, select the final architectural register-write value from the
extracted load data or EX/MEM ALU/link result before the MEM/WB clock
edge. Store that selected 32-bit value in one authoritative result
register. WB's data output and WB-to-EX bypass then read it directly,
eliminating the late ctrl.mem_to_reg mux from the execute input path.
Reuse the existing MEM/WB alu_result storage for this final value,
retaining its field name, packed position and width. The separate
read_data field can remain for layout compatibility but must not create
a second selected WB data path. Update the comments to express the
new selected-result meaning of the MEM/WB alu_result field.
EX/MEM.alu_result retains its existing meaning and still provides the
younger ALU bypass. On every accepted MEM capture, MEM/WB alu_result is
mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result. On a genuine data-memory hold,
retain this selected value, destination and write eligibility and clear only
retirement valid. This preserves older-load bypass during prolonged
holds. Keep regfile write-first bypass and RVFI rd_wdata on the exact
same WB data wire. Preserve load lane extraction, all alignment traps
and every memory handshake; add no retirement or load-use cycle.

Give the selector registers synchronous reset and the same true hold as
ID/EX. Squash and missing fetch readiness affect only instruction valid,
never raw source addresses or the selector/payload capture enable. During
a data-memory hold, EX/MEM holds its data/tag and MEM/WB retains its data,
tag and bypass eligibility while clearing only retirement valid; holding
the selectors therefore preserves the selected source until acceptance.
During a divider wait, the launched divide already owns captured actual
operands. Keep that launch-time capture, eight-edge schedule, sticky
completion and result consume behavior exactly intact; draining older
stages must not cause the divide to relaunch or reinterpret changing
bypass values. The next instruction's fresh selectors are captured only
when the divide result advances. Reset cancels selector and divider state.

Keep static backward-taken/JAL prediction, one-bit recovery, the explicit
flip-flop RF with write-first bypass, all arithmetic and ALTOPS formulas,
trap discipline, nret=1 ports, exact-once memory effects and contiguous
in-order RVFI retirement. Selector metadata may be separate sideband
registers to preserve existing packed bundle offsets and prediction-bit
position. Keep kill independent of wide payload and selector enables.
Producer eligibility must include every existing trap suppression; an
illegal or misaligned write must never become a preselected dependency.

Run unchanged formal, ALU, RF and pipeline checks and extend pipeline
coverage for youngest-writer priority, both operands selecting different
stages, x0, immediate load-use replay, invalid writing payloads, trapped
producers, prolonged memory holds retaining WB bypass, divide launch
from both bypass sources, consecutive divides, reset and branch recovery.
Check architectural RVFI operands/results and single memory side effects.
Keep the ready-high ten-clock branch-to-divide bound and all existing
timing assertions. Canonical stalled CoreMark should retain 4,259,699
marked cycles and all five CRCs plus the required UART validation text.
Evaluate all three Gowin placement options and verify destination-tag
comparison no longer shares a path with EX arithmetic. With unchanged
cycles the acceptance threshold is above 54.06 MHz median Fmax. The
complete probe's 56.328 MHz median clears it by a useful margin; its
option-0 result is lower, so all three placement options matter.
Option 0 used 4,338 logic cells, 1,501 registers, four BSRAMs and six
DSPs. Its worst path now starts at a registered bypass selector and
reaches divider launch in 24.472 ns through 21 cells; producer-tag
comparison and the WB load/ALU mux are absent from that path. The
remaining risks are placement sensitivity, timing moving to early
eligibility, load-result selection or divider arithmetic, and errors
associating preselection with held instructions.

The complete temporary RTL prototype passed the existing pipeline
suite, eight full-RVFI selftest/random-program comparisons with and

wrapper. Actual M arithmetic is unchanged and exercised by cosim;

and vendor fitness measurement. Only the hypothesis YAML is delivered;
