title: Static-biased exception predictor with deferred training
motivation:
The current backward-taken/JAL predictor reaches 121.32 iterations/sec
at 51.68 MHz and 4,259,699 marked CoreMark cycles. Prior 64-entry bimodal
predictors used 4,201,740 cycles but lost enough Fmax to regress. A new
predictor must preserve the cheap static default and keep live EX
resolution out of direction-storage feedback rather than repeat that
table. A small cache of recurring exceptions is a more selective way
to recover forward-taken and backward-not-taken branch slots.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the existing aligned B/J target calculation, always-taken JAL,
sequential JALR, and one-bit direct-control recovery. Add one eight-entry
direct-mapped direction-exception cache for conditional branches only.
Index with PC[4:2], compare a full PC[31:5] tag, and hold a valid bit and
two-bit confidence counter per entry. A cache miss keeps backward-taken /
forward-not-taken prediction. A matching entry predicts the opposite of
the instruction's static direction only while confidence has its high
bit set. Tags are performance metadata; instruction predecode and
alignment checks remain mandatory before any prediction is enabled.

Train confidence on whether the resolved direction differs from the
instruction's static direction. Increment with saturation for an
exception and decrement with saturation for agreement. Allocate a
nonmatching entry only on an exception, initialized strongly toward the
observed exception; do not replace a useful exception entry on an
ordinary static-correct branch. Invalidate a matching entry when its
counter reaches zero. Reset valid bits and pending-update validity;
payload need not be reset because lookup always checks validity.
Describe storage as eight fixed flip-flop words with decoded write
enables and a balanced masked-OR read, avoiding a target RAM or BSRAM.

Register the accepted EX update event, branch PC, and exception bit,
and apply the cache update on the following edge. All tag/counter
read-modify-write logic consumes these registers, not live forwarded
operands or redirect. Capture one update exactly when a legal aligned
conditional branch advances: in.valid && !reset && !stall_ex_mem &&
!divider_wait. Pending events drain independently of subsequent bus
stalls; a held branch cannot generate duplicate updates. One-cycle
training delay affects accuracy only. Keep the exact predicted_taken
bit captured with each instruction; EX must never reconstruct it from
a later lookup. Use existing one-bit mismatch correction and resolved
RVFI next PC, including sequential recovery on a trap.

This is one direction-prediction change. Preserve nret=1, all ports,
raw instruction/source-address paths, validity-only squash, forwarding,
retained WB bypass data, divider timing and ALTOPS behavior, decoder
legality, misalignment traps, and exact-once memory/retirement effects.
Validate cache misses, both static directions, confidence saturation,
conflicting full tags, replacement, update delay, back-to-back branches,
reset with a pending update, and correction overlapping instruction,
data, load-use, and divider waits. Retain all existing tests and run
unchanged formal/cosim plus canonical marker-bracketed CoreMark and
median Gowin timing. The estimated overall gain depends on containing
lookup/update timing costs; no FPGA gain has yet been measured.

title: Two narrow radix-4 decisions for divider launch
motivation:
The champion's median Fmax is 56.328 MHz at 4,259,699 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its reported worst path starts at the registered rs2 bypass
selector and ends at divider launch remainder bit 2, with 24.472 ns
arrival and 21 cells. The launch still performs four serial restoring
decisions and derives their divisor-width guards after full-width
signed normalization. Earlier carry-select trial subtractors regressed;
a Boolean nibble lookup helped an older champion but moved the limit
to forwarding and multiplication, while a larger prefix ROM inferred
extra BSRAM. With forwarding decisions and the final WB result now
registered, the remaining launch logic is a concrete timing target.

An isolated prototype of this exact launch rewrite produced vendor
placement Fmax values 57.843, 59.538 and 59.538 MHz, median 59.538 MHz.
Stalled canonical CoreMark passed the evaluator's unchanged CRC, UART,
bounded-access, termination and marker checks with exactly 4,259,699
marked cycles. Prototype fitness is 139.77 iterations/sec, 5.7 percent
above 132.23 and above the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's median Fmax is 56.328 MHz at 4,259,699 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its reported worst path starts at the registered rs2 bypass
selector and ends at divider launch remainder bit 2, with 24.472 ns
arrival and 21 cells. The launch still performs four serial restoring
decisions and derives their divisor-width guards after full-width
signed normalization. Earlier carry-select trial subtractors regressed;
a Boolean nibble lookup helped an older champion but moved the limit
to forwarding and multiplication, while a larger prefix ROM inferred
extra BSRAM. With forwarding decisions and the final WB result now
registered, the remaining launch logic is a concrete timing target.

An isolated prototype of this exact launch rewrite produced vendor
placement Fmax values 57.843, 59.538 and 59.538 MHz, median 59.538 MHz.
Stalled canonical CoreMark passed the evaluator's unchanged CRC, UART,

marked cycles. Prototype fitness is 139.77 iterations/sec, 5.7 percent

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the divider's combinational four-bit launch prefix.
Replace its four dependent radix-2 subtract-and-restore decisions with
two narrow radix-4 decisions, using three parallel trial subtractions
and balanced selection at each decision. Derive the bounded prefix
inputs directly from raw operands so no full-width magnitude-negation
carry chain feeds the prefix. Retain launch plus seven busy edges,
the existing full-width busy recurrence, registered divisor multiples,
sticky result-valid/consume behavior, and every pipeline control.

Let neg_a and neg_b be signed_op AND the corresponding operand sign.
The normalized dividend's top nibble P is a[31:28] for !neg_a, or
(~a[31:28]) + (a[27:0] == 0) in explicit four-bit modular arithmetic
for neg_a. The normalized divisor's low nibble d is b[3:0] for !neg_b,
or (~b[3:0]) + 1 in explicit four-bit arithmetic for neg_b. Determine
small_d, meaning the full unsigned divisor magnitude is less than 16,
directly: !neg_b ? !(|b[31:4]) : ((&b[31:4]) && b[3:0] != 0).
This correctly rejects -16 and INT_MIN without waiting for -b.
Full magnitude_a and magnitude_b remain available independently for
the ordinary launch-state registers; do not change their arithmetic.

Precompute the unsigned six-bit multiples m1={2'b0,d}, m2=m1<<1,
and m3=m1+m2. Decision zero consumes P[3:2], so its trial/remainder
width W is 2. Decision one consumes {R0,P[1:0]}, with W=4. At each
decision compute T-m1, T-m2 and T-m3 in parallel using W+1-bit
zero-extended subtractions of the low W multiple bits. Multiple k fits
only if small_d is true, all multiple bits above W-1 are zero, and
the subtraction's borrow bit W is clear. These high-bit guards are
mandatory; truncated multiples alone are incorrect for d near 15.
Encode the largest fitting digit as q[1]=fit2 and
q[0]=fit3 || (!fit2 && fit1), then select the corresponding low-W
remainder or unchanged T with two balanced mux levels. For D>=16,
force both quotient digits to zero and pass the consumed prefix as
remainder. For D=0 all trials fit, naturally producing digit 3 at
each decision and retaining P as remainder. Concatenate the two
quotient digits into Q and retain the four-bit final remainder R.
Launch quotient_q with {magnitude_a[27:0],Q} and remainder_q with
{28'b0,R}, exactly reproducing the existing four prefix steps.

Use explicit small-width arithmetic and generate wiring. Do not use
variable division, remainder operators, case-table ROMs, or additional
pipeline registers. This hypothesis shortens a local arithmetic cone;
it does not retime stages, change execution latency, or add a predictor.
Preserve DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU semantics for zero divisors, INT_MIN/-1,
high unsigned operands, signed truncation and remainder signs. Keep
every ALTOPS expression and its eight-edge handshake unchanged, along
with nret=1, decoder/trap checks, memory handshakes and RVFI ordering.

Validate the prefix exhaustively for all nibble pairs and large-divisor
guards against independent integer arithmetic. Exercise actual RV32M
arithmetic with signed boundary and seeded random operands, existing
ALU and pipeline tests, reset and held results, cosim and the unchanged
formal gates. Canonical stalled CoreMark should retain exactly
4,259,699 marked cycles and all required CRCs/UART validation. Measure
all three vendor placement options: unchanged cycles require a median
above 58.920 MHz to exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. The
measured prototype gain is 5.7 percent from Fmax. Placement option 0
uses 4,250 logic cells, 1,501 registers, zero LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs
and six DSPs. Its worst arrival is 22.583 ns through 12 cells; the
divider launch is no longer the worst path, and the new limit crosses
forwarding/multiplication to the data-memory input. Keep the proposal
confined to the launch rewrite; all three placement options matter.

The prototype passed the unchanged ALU and pipeline suites plus an
additional 4,128 directed actual-arithmetic division/remainder checks,
including every prefix/divisor nibble pair and signed normalization
boundaries. An independent launch model passed 21,934 comparisons.
The local real-arithmetic SAT proof passed after mechanically replacing
its old launch_remainder[4] reference with the new final remainder
signal: retain the exact Q*D+R prefix identity, R<D and zero-divisor
assertions and both unchanged full-width recurrence assertions. No
proof property or constraint may be weakened. Both real and ALTOPS
lint passed, and all eight full-RVFI selftest/random-program cosim runs
passed with and without instruction/data stalls. All 53 original
single-retire ALTOPS formal tasks passed using an isolated staging
directory and the original wrapper/check configuration. Formal-deep
was not run; the separate local SAT proof checks the actual divider
arithmetic without ALTOPS. These are isolated prototype results; the
implementation must still rerun the gates and vendor fitness
measurement. Only this hypothesis YAML is delivered.

title: Register M-extension operands before arithmetic execution
motivation:
The champion reaches 132.23 iterations/sec at 56.328 MHz and 4,259,699
marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a registered bypass
selector and ends in divider initialization, at 24.472 ns through 21
cells. The prior structural divider-initialization experiment removed
that path but exposed forwarding through multiplication to the memory
address, and its four-bit truth table inferred an extra BSRAM. Moving
only one arithmetic cone leaves the other constraining every clock.
A common operand-capture boundary for blocking M execution should
separate forwarding from both expensive arithmetic networks.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 132.23 iterations/sec at 56.328 MHz and 4,259,699
marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a registered bypass
selector and ends in divider initialization, at 24.472 ns through 21
cells. The prior structural divider-initialization experiment removed
that path but exposed forwarding through multiplication to the memory
address, and its four-bit truth table inferred an extra BSRAM. Moving
only one arithmetic cone leaves the other constraining every clock.
A common operand-capture boundary for blocking M execution should
separate forwarding from both expensive arithmetic networks.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Place the real M-extension execution datapaths behind a registered
request boundary in EX. Ordinary RV32I instructions retain their
current pipeline and latency. A valid MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU or
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU captures its forwarded operands and operation once,
holds ID/EX and fetch until completion, drains older stages once, and
injects invalid EX/MEM bubbles while waiting. Only genuine downstream
memory backpressure retains EX/MEM. Preserve launch, sticky completion,
consume, reset cancellation, and original launch-time RVFI operands.
This is one structural change to the operand boundary of M execution;
do not add a general pipeline stage or change branch prediction.

For multiplication, capture the raw 32-bit operands and operation on
edge 1, then register the selected architectural product on edge 2.
Instantiate multiplication only from these request registers, rather
than the live EX forwarding mux outputs. Preserve exact low and high
halves for all signed/unsigned variants; reuse the existing three
Gowin-inferable product expressions with registered operand inputs.
Keep product sign selection driven by registered op. Keep the operand,
product and handshake registers inside alu.sv so its existing product
structure and DSP mapping are retained.
Accept the result into EX/MEM on the following available edge. This
adds two blocked cycles to multiplication relative to today's live
combinational multiply but removes its DSP/correction/result-selection
chain from forwarding-to-memory timing. Do not duplicate a live
multiplier in the ordinary ALU result cone.

For division, retain exactly eight edges from accepted launch to
result_valid. Edge 1 captures unsigned magnitudes, sign metadata and
operation; perform neither prefix quotient work nor 3D generation
on that edge. Edge 2 consumes the first eight dividend bits using
only registered magnitudes and registers Q, R, D and 34-bit 3D.
Implement the first four quotient bits as explicit Boolean/narrow
arithmetic logic rather than a dynamic-index ROM or 256-entry case
table. Use the exact arithmetic truth functions of
x={D[3:0],A[31:28]}: for nonzero D<16, Q=P/D and R=P%D;
for D=0, Q=15 and R=P. Enumerate the 256 constant input pairs offline,
minimize each of the eight output bits into explicit AND/OR equations,
and emit no synthesizable division, remainder, table or memory lookup.
A deterministic minimization merges cubes differing in one specified
bit, retains prime implicants, selects all essentials, then greedily
covers remaining minterms by most uncovered points, fewest literals,
and ascending (value,mask). This produces 21,22,17,8 product terms
for R[0:3] and 27,10,4,2 for Q[0:3]. Override this nibble result with
Q=0,R=P if D[31:4] is nonzero. Append the next four bits with two
tapered radix-4 decisions
at widths 6 and 8. Narrow divisor multiples must retain all required
high-bit guards; D above 255 yields Q_prefix=0 and R_prefix=A[31:24].
Generate the full-width 3D register input in parallel with the prefix,
never as an input to its narrow decision chain. Initialize
Q={A[23:0],Q_prefix[7:0]} and R={24'b0,R_prefix[7:0]}.
Edges 3 through 8 retain the existing two full-width radix-4 digit
decisions per edge, consuming the remaining 24 bits. Keep quotient
and remainder sign correction from completed registered state.
Preserve zero-divisor results, signed truncation toward zero, the
dividend's sign for remainder, and INT_MIN/-1 exactly. Do not add
setup or correction edges to division or relax the existing ten-clock
ready-high branch-to-divide successor-retirement check.

Keep the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas behind matching request
and completion schedules for both M operation groups. Hold captured
requests and results independently of changing live bypass data and
bus readiness. Consume only when EX/MEM can advance; never relaunch
a held operation or retire it twice. A killed or invalid M opcode
must not launch either engine. Retain the registered bypass selectors,
preselected MEM/WB result, retained WB forwarding data during stalls,
validity-only squash, load-use replay, nret=1 ports, default-illegal
decoder behavior, alignment traps and contiguous in-order RVFI.

Run the unchanged formal and cosim gates and retain every arithmetic
expected-value check. Extend directed pipeline coverage for every MUL
variant from both bypass sources, immediate multiply dependents,
multiply-to-load/store/branch, consecutive mixed M operations, changing
live operands while busy, blocked result consumption, wrong-path M
instructions and reset in either phase. Arithmetic unit tests should
exercise the explicit request/response handshake without relaxing
correctness, division latency, sticky-result or reset assertions.
Verify the eight-bit prefix identity and remainder bound independently,
including all small divisors, high-divisor guards and divide by zero.
Check canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs, UART validation and marker-only
timing, then evaluate median Gowin Fmax times iterations/cycle.

Expected benefit is higher Fmax at a modest multiplication-cycle cost.
The remaining divider recurrence, RF read network and prefix routing
can limit the gain; multiplication frequency determines the IPC cost.
At unchanged cycles the acceptance threshold is approximately 58.92
MHz; use the actual increased marked cycle count when comparing against
the 132.23 champion and 4.6% gate.

A complete isolated RTL prototype of this boundary change passed all
30 existing ALU cases, all 34 existing pipeline cases, and eight
full-RVFI comparisons of selftest/random programs with ready-high and
randomized instruction/data buses. The unchanged 53-task ALTOPS formal
suite passed in a private staging tree using the original single-retire
wrapper, checks, depths and assumptions. Division still completes on
edge eight and the existing branch-to-divide bound passes. CoreMark
with both bus stalls completed in 4,446,945 marker-bracketed cycles,
a 4.40% increase, with no out-of-bounds accesses, all five canonical
CRCs and the required validation text.

Additional tests passed 128 randomized multiplier requests with live
operand/op mutation and sticky-result relaunch attempts, and 16 mixed
multiply/load/store/divide dependency programs spanning all four MUL
variants and four bus-stall settings. A local Yosys SAT proof without
ALTOPS passed the complete eight-bit prefix identity and remainder
bound for arbitrary registered operands, the zero-divisor prefix
identity, and both original full-width recurrence identities. Existing
unit arithmetic expected values and completion deadlines were retained;
only the internal edge-1 prefix identity now reflects zero bits consumed.

Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 57.919/63.801/63.801 MHz, giving
63.801 MHz median and implied fitness 143.47 iterations/sec, 8.50%
above the 132.23 champion. The frequency increase outweighs the added
multiplication cycles. At this cycle count acceptance requires over
61.507 MHz median. Option 0 used 4,433 logic cells, 1,542 registers,
zero LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs. Its worst path is now wholly
inside the divider, from registered divisor to remainder, at 22.560
ns; the bypass-to-divider-launch and live multiplier paths are absent.
These are temporary prototype results, not an implemented tournament
candidate. Implementation must reproduce the boundary and rerun the
unchanged evaluator gates. No repository RTL or contract files were
modified, and the slow full-core formal-deep suite was not run.

title: Prediction-guided fetch lookahead during pipeline stalls
motivation:
The champion's stateless backward-taken/JAL predictor avoids most direct
control bubbles, but prediction advances fetch only when ID/EX accepts
an instruction. During load-use and data-memory stalls, ready instruction
bus cycles are discarded. After the hold ends, a new instruction-bus
stall can then add another bubble. Prior dynamic direction predictors
saved only 0.8-1.4% additional CoreMark cycles and sacrificed Fmax; use
the existing cheap prediction to fetch ahead instead of adding another
branch direction table. A canonical reference profile found 544,852
loads and 204,039 immediately following raw load-use dependencies inside
the timing markers, providing substantial opportunities for lookahead.
A one-slot RTL prototype reduced marked cycles to 4,088,712 but reached
only 45.445 MHz median Gowin Fmax. A two-slot prototype improved marked
cycles to 4,056,799 versus the champion's 4,259,699, a 5.00% throughput
gain at equal Fmax. It reached 54.713 MHz median Fmax, or about 134.87
iterations/sec, only 2.00% above 132.23. The proposal therefore needs
a compact implementation that recovers timing; it is not a measured
qualifying improvement. With these cycles the 4.6% margin requires
approximately 56.12 MHz, close to the champion's 56.328 MHz.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple predictor-directed instruction acquisition from ID/EX admission
with a two-entry fall-through fetched-instruction queue. Keep the current static
legal/aligned B/J prediction and one-bit EX recovery. The instruction bus
has its own fetch PC. When the queue has space and io_imemReady is high,
accept the actual bus instruction and advance that fetch PC using its
predicted target or PC+4, even if a load-use, data-memory or divider hold
prevents decode admission. Store the fetched PC, instruction and exact
predicted_taken bit in the queue. This is one predictor-guided lookahead
mechanism; no new direction table, data prediction or cache is needed.

When empty, bypass a ready bus response directly to decode to preserve
the current zero-hold latency. If decode cannot consume that response,
capture it and advance the fetch PC. When occupied, decode sees the slot
rather than the bus; consuming its head can simultaneously replace it
with a ready response at the current predicted successor PC. The tail
holds a second response; consuming a two-entry queue promotes the tail
and can simultaneously refill it. When full and held, preserve both
entries and fetch PC and ignore unaccepted bus data. A pop without a
replacement decreases occupancy while holding the bus fetch PC. Never use data from a
cycle with io_imemReady=0. Buffered instructions remain valid for decode
even when the current bus response is not ready.

Feed hazard detection, register-file read addresses and ID decode from
the selected head instruction. Distinguish head availability from raw
instruction-bus readiness: an unavailable new response must not stall a
valid buffered head. ID/EX admission still obeys existing load-use,
data-memory and divider holds. Capture its prediction bit with the head;
do not recompute prediction from the separately advanced bus PC. Retain
the registered forwarding decisions and validity-only ID/EX squash.

An accepted EX correction has highest priority over head consumption,
replacement and ordinary holds: invalidate all buffered wrong-path data
and set the bus fetch PC to the resolved recovery target. An older data
stall defers that correction as today. Reset clears slot validity and
restores fetch PC zero. Both queued instructions and a simultaneous bus
response must be discarded on correction; neither may enter ID/EX or
perform a memory effect. Every instruction admitted to ID/EX must have
been obtained from an accepted imem response at its own captured PC.

Use two fixed FF payload banks with head-valid and tail-valid bits and
explicit write enables. Reset only these valid bits and the bus fetch
PC; leave payload unreset because valid bits gate all architectural use.
Keep tail_valid implies head_valid, and define decode consumption as
!stall_if && !redirect, with response acceptance io_imemReady &&
(!tail_valid || consumption) && !redirect. On an empty queue, a consumed
response bypasses without being enqueued; an unconsumed accepted response
fills the head. Retain the existing predictor
target arithmetic, and avoid adding a sequential stage on the empty
bypass path. Keep nret=1, top-level ports, all decoder/alignment/trap
behavior, arithmetic and ALTOPS, retained WB forwarding, exact-once
memory effects and contiguous architectural RVFI retirement. RVFI PCs
come from the consumed head and resolved EX next PC, never the lookahead
bus PC. The predicted path may be fetched early but cannot retire early.

Validate empty bypass, capture under every hold reason, head consumption
while imem is stalled, simultaneous pop/refill, full-slot hold, reset,
correctly predicted consecutive branches/JALs, loop exits and JALR
corrections with full and empty slots. Combine correction with imem
stalls, load-use dependencies and older dmem holds; check exact-once
retirement and stores, source values, PC continuity and canonical CRCs.
Run the unchanged formal/cosim gates and score marker-bracketed CoreMark
cycles times median Gowin Fmax. Update old bus-PC-hold observations to
assert fetch-PC advancement only on accepted responses or corrections
and full-queue holds, preserving every ID/EX hold, forwarding, retirement,
reset and memory-effect assertion. Two original tests assume bus PC
equals the blocked decode PC and must observe the head separately.
The main risks are added head-mux timing
into decode/RF and queue control placement. Measured RTL and FPGA results
must establish whether saved overlap exceeds the 4.6% acceptance margin.

title: Fuse narrow and full-width divider digit pairs
motivation:
The champion achieves 143.74 iterations/sec at 63.920 MHz with
4,446,945 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path
runs wholly inside the registered divider, from divisor_q[27] to
remainder_q[0], with 20 cells and 21.764 ns arrival. Request registers
have already removed the live forwarding and multiplication paths.
A reproduced vendor report shows that this path actually crosses the
eight-bit initialization prefix: the wide divisor guard feeds nibble
selection and both narrow radix-4 decisions. The later full-width
recurrence also contains two dependent radix-4 subtract/select decisions
per clock. Earlier micro_opt experiments
addressed launch normalization or forwarding, and the r2s0 segmented
carry-select attempt regressed by 22.46%; repeating those changes
does not directly eliminate this serial decision dependency.
The current 4,391 logic cells leave room to trade parallel arithmetic
for a shorter recurrence without adding division or pipeline cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Fuse each pair of radix-4 digit decisions inside the real divider into
one parallel radix-16 trial bank. Apply the same arithmetic optimization
to the final four bits of the edge-2 initialization prefix and to every
four-bit recurrence on edges 3 through 8. This is a local
arithmetic reorganization inside divider.sv, not a change to pipeline
topology, fetch prediction, issue width, or the M-engine handshake.
Keep edge 1 magnitude capture and edge 2 eight-bit prefix initialization,
and still consume exactly four dividend bits on each subsequent edge.
Completion must remain on edge eight with the existing sticky result.

First eliminate the serial narrow decisions in edge 2. Retain the
existing explicit Boolean nibble truth functions, but evaluate this
helper against D8=D[7:0]. Its nibble override tests D8[7:4], rather
than propagating D[31:8] through the arithmetic chain. Form the
eight-bit T8={nibble_remainder,A[27:24]}. Compute all k*D8 multiples
exactly at 12 unsigned bits for k=1..15, using shifted D8, independent
odd-multiple sums and carry-save compression for three-term sums.
Evaluate thirteen-bit zero-extended T8-k*D8 trials in parallel, derive
adjacent-fit one-hot selectors, and use balanced masked-OR trees for
the eight-bit remainder and four-bit digit. Concatenate the Boolean
nibble quotient and the new digit into Q_prefix. Qualify the complete
byte-prefix result once at the final output: if D[31:8]!=0, force
Q_prefix=0 and R_prefix=A[31:24]; otherwise use the computed result.
This is exact because any D>=256 exceeds the complete dividend prefix.
Keep 12 bits for multiples and 13 for borrow tests: truncated eight-bit
multiples would falsely fit. No new prefix lookup memory is permitted.

For the later recurrence's registered Q, R and unsigned divisor D,
form the 36-bit unsigned
T={R,Q[31:28]}. Register exact 36-bit odd multiples D,3D,5D,7D,9D,
11D,13D,15D on edge 2, in parallel with the existing narrow prefix.
Derive even multiples from these registers by constant left shifts:
kD = odd_part(k)D << trailing_zero_count(k). Powers of two are shifts
of D. All multiple storage, shifts and arithmetic must be 36-bit
unsigned; neither 15D nor T may be truncated to 32 or 34 bits.
Generate odd multiples directly from captured D and shifted copies,
never by a serial chain of previous multiple sums. Two-term sums and
15D=(D<<4)-D use one carry-propagating operation; three-term 7D,11D,
13D may use an explicit carry-save compressor followed by one final
carry-propagating add. No multiple generation may feed the recurrence
combinationally; it must finish before its edge-2 register boundary.
Avoid dynamic-index tables, division operators, and new inferred RAMs.

Compute all fifteen {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,kD} trials independently at 37
bits for k=1..15. Define fit[k]=!difference[k][36], fit[0]=1 and
fit[16]=0. Obtain a one-hot winning digit with
select[k]=fit[k] && !fit[k+1], k=0..15. The exact, ordered multiples
make the fit vector monotonic. For D=0 all fits are true, so digit 15
wins and the remainder naturally retains the incoming dividend prefix.
Select the new remainder with an explicit balanced masked-OR tree
of sixteen 32-bit candidates: T[31:0] for digit zero and each trial's
low 32 bits for digits 1..15. Encode the four quotient bits by balanced
OR reductions over the corresponding one-hot selectors, then set
Q_next={Q[27:0],digit}. Avoid a priority if/case chain or a final
digit-times-divisor multiply followed by another serial subtraction.
The invariant R<D for D!=0 ensures that the winning remainder fits
in 32 bits; keep all 36 bits through fit decisions before truncation.

Retain signed magnitude/sign-correction logic,
all divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 behavior, request acceptance, reset
cancellation, consume-plus-launch behavior, and launch-time RVFI data.
Keep the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and its eight-edge schedule;
exclude the real trial bank and its registers from ALTOPS builds.
Preserve every existing arithmetic, latency, progress, trap, bus-stall,
in-order retirement and nret=1 check. Only divider arithmetic and
focused additional arithmetic tests are in scope.

Verify equivalence of one radix-16 step to two radix-4 steps using
independent integer references for every quotient digit and boundaries
T=kD-1,kD,kD+1, including high-bit divisors and maximal legal R.
Prove complete byte-prefix equivalence for arbitrary captured A and D,
including the late wide-divisor override. Exercise D=0 separately and
test all RV32M signed corners. Extend the
existing ALU suite without weakening its edge-by-edge prefix/remainder
identities, exact eight-edge deadline or sticky-result assertions.
Run existing formal and cosim gates, canonical stalled CoreMark CRC
and UART checks, and vendor timing. At unchanged marked cycles, a
median Fmax above 66.86 MHz clears the 4.6% acceptance threshold.
Expect identical CoreMark cycles and higher Fmax from eliminating the
first remainder mux and second dependent wide subtract/fit cone.
Increased subtractor count, selector fanout and routing congestion are
the main risks. Fusing only the full-width recurrence left the old
prefix critical and measured 57.233 MHz median; the final proposal
fuses both digit pairs so neither retains that dependency. The final
isolated prototype passed all 32 existing ALU cases and all 38 existing
pipeline cases. A Yosys SAT equivalence check proved its complete
eight-bit prefix identical to the champion for arbitrary 32-bit
magnitudes. A bit-accurate arithmetic model passed 483,500 radix-16
step comparisons and 41,600 complete RV32M comparisons against
independent integer arithmetic. These checks do not replace the
implementing agent's unchanged formal, cosim and vendor evaluation.

The final isolated RTL prototype also passed eight full-RVFI trace
comparisons: selftest and the three existing random programs, each
with ready-high and randomized instruction/data buses. Canonical
stalled CoreMark completed in exactly 4,446,945 marker-bracketed cycles,
with no out-of-bounds accesses, all five expected CRCs and the required
validation text. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured
67.711/71.747/71.747 MHz, giving a 71.747 MHz median and implied fitness
161.34 iterations/sec, approximately 12.24% above the 143.74 champion.
Option 0 used 5,562 logic cells, 1,775 registers, zero LUT-RAMs, four
BSRAMs and six DSPs. Its worst path moved out of the divider to the
WB-forwarded JALR/PC redirect path, with 20.063 ns arrival. These are
private prototype measurements; the implementing agent must reproduce
the specified arithmetic and rerun the unchanged evaluator gates.
The full-core formal-deep suite was not run.

title: Replace serial divider digits with a parallel radix-16 recurrence
motivation:
The champion scores 143.74 iterations/sec at 63.920 MHz with 4,446,945
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path is now wholly inside
the divider, from divisor_q to remainder_q, at 21.764 ns through 20
cells. Registered M operands removed the live forwarding and multiply
bottlenecks. The remaining recurrence still serializes two full-width
radix-4 subtract/select decisions in every arithmetic clock. Prior
structural attempts succeeded by removing dependent arithmetic from
a clock interval; changing fetch or bypass logic no longer addresses
the measured limiting path.

marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path is now wholly inside
the divider, from divisor_q to remainder_q, at 21.764 ns through 20
cells. Registered M operands removed the live forwarding and multiply

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the divider around one parallel radix-16 digit decision
instead of two dependent radix-4 subtract/select decisions. Apply
this topology to both the four-bit recurrence and the second nibble
of prefix initialization. Preserve the existing eight-edge
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU schedule: edge 1 captures magnitudes and metadata,
edge 2 computes the guarded eight-bit prefix and initializes divisor
multiples, and edges 3 through 8 consume the remaining 24 bits.
Preserve multiplication, the ordinary pipeline, branch prediction,
registered forwarding, top-level ports and nret=1.

Form the unsigned 36-bit trial dividend T={R,Q[31:28]}. Register
exact divisor multiples needed for all digits 1 through 15 before
the first recurrence edge. Use constant shifts of registered odd
multiples for even multiples where this avoids redundant storage.
All multiples must retain 36 bits; neither a high-bit divisor nor
a multiple larger than UINT_MAX may be truncated before comparison.
Compute all fifteen T-kD trial differences concurrently at 37 bits,
deriving fit[k] from the unsigned borrow bit. These subtractors read
registered state and registered multiples only. No candidate may
depend on another candidate's subtraction or selected remainder.

Encode the largest fitting digit without a fifteen-deep priority
chain. Fits are monotonic: choose[k]=fit[k]&&!fit[k+1] for k=1..14,
choose[15]=fit[15], and choose[0]=!fit[1]. Generate each quotient
digit bit by a balanced OR of the corresponding choose terms. Select
the low 32-bit remainder with one-hot masking of the sixteen
candidates and an explicit balanced reduction tree, or an equally
shallow balanced selection network. Update Q={Q[27:0],digit} and
R=selected_remainder. For D!=0 the selected remainder is below D;
for D=0 every trial fits, digit 15 is selected and the dividend
prefix remains the remainder. Preserve quotient sign suppression
for zero divisors, signed truncation toward zero, dividend-signed
remainder, and INT_MIN/-1 exactly.

Prepare multiples outside the recurrence. Capture odd multiples
3D,5D,7D,9D,11D,13D,15D on edge 2 from the registered magnitude D.
Use exact shift/add or shift/subtract constant arithmetic; independent
constant expressions must not become a serial running sum of D.
This work runs in parallel with the prefix and must not feed its
decision chain. Check its timing as well as the recurrence; multiple
generation, subtractor fanout and wide selection routing are the
principal risks. Avoid tables, inferred ROMs or extra memory blocks.

Prefix initialization must not retain its two serial radix-4 stages,
since that becomes the timing limit after parallelizing recurrence.
Keep the existing Boolean first-nibble Q/R equations. On edge 1 also
capture small4_q=!(|magnitude_b[31:4]) and
small8_q=!(|magnitude_b[31:8]) from the accepted magnitude, alongside
divisor_q. These flags remain associated with that request through
completion and reset inactive. At edge 2 use small4_q to select
Q_first=small4_q?nibble_q:0 and
R_first=small4_q?nibble_r:A[31:28]. Do not put a fresh 28-bit divisor
reduction ahead of the Boolean nibble and following arithmetic.
Form the eight-bit prefix trial T_prefix={R_first,A[27:24]}.
In parallel compute fifteen exact 12-bit constant multiples
M_prefix[k]={4'b0,D[7:0]}*12'(k) and nine-bit trial differences
{1'b0,T_prefix}-{1'b0,M_prefix[k][7:0]}. A prefix digit fits only
when small8_q is true, M_prefix[k][11:8] is zero and the difference
has no borrow. This prevents truncated multiples from falsely fitting.
Use the same monotonic fit/one-hot choose/balanced selection structure
at eight-bit width, yielding the second four-bit prefix quotient
digit and eight-bit remainder. Set
Q={A[23:0],Q_first,second_digit} and R={24'b0,R_prefix} on edge 2.
D=0 yields both prefix digits equal to 15 and R_prefix=A[31:24].
Preserve the registered classifier association rather than moving
first-nibble arithmetic back onto the live forwarded operand path.

Keep the existing launch/busy/sticky-result/consume interface,
reset cancellation, captured RVFI operands, exact-once retirement,
older-stage draining and memory-backpressure priorities. Keep the
exact ALTOPS formulas and identical eight-edge completion deadline
in formal builds. Do not add setup, correction or iteration edges,
relax formal depths or the ten-clock branch-to-divide bound, alter
decoder legality or change any evaluation contract file.

Validate the radix-16 recurrence identity and 32-bit remainder bound
independently, including all digit boundaries, high-bit divisors,
zero divisors and signed corner cases. Retain and run all existing
arithmetic, handshake, pipeline and formal checks. Verify canonical
stalled CoreMark CRCs, validation text, memory bounds and marker-only
cycle count. The expected cycle count is unchanged. Compare median
vendor Gowin Fmax times iterations/cycle against 143.74; at unchanged
cycles acceptance requires more than approximately 66.86 MHz.
An isolated prototype of the full-width and narrow radix-16 topology
with captured divisor-width flags measured 72.692/76.151/76.151 MHz
for Gowin placement options 0/1/2: median 76.151 MHz, approximately
19.1% above the champion's frequency. Option 0 used 5,436 logic cells,
1,750 registers, zero LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and seven DSPs. The worst
option-0 path moved to forwarded base-ALU execution feeding dmem at
19.051 ns; a divider prefix path was nearly tied at 19.048 ns.
Prototype measurements are evidence for this hypothesis, not an
implemented tournament candidate; implementation must reproduce
the complete structure and rerun the unchanged evaluator gates.

The final isolated prototype passed all 33 existing ALU cocotb cases,
all 38 existing pipeline cases, and all 53 unchanged single-retire
ALTOPS formal tasks in private staging with the original wrapper,
configuration, depths and assumptions. Eight full-RVFI cosim runs
passed for selftest and three random instruction programs, each with

Local Yosys SAT checks without ALTOPS proved the parallel eight-bit

Canonical CoreMark with both randomized bus stalls passed UART/CRC,

title: Four-entry predictor-directed fetch lookahead
motivation:
Static backward-taken/JAL prediction already captures most CoreMark branch
locality. Earlier direction tables saved only about one additional percent
of cycles and reduced FPGA clock frequency. The previous two-entry fetch
lookahead saved about five percent of cycles on the older champion. The
current champion registers M-extension requests and spends two additional
cycles waiting for each multiply, providing more opportunities to acquire
instructions along the existing predicted path during execution holds.

An isolated four-entry fall-through queue prototype on the exact current
champion completed canonical stalled CoreMark in 4,111,263 marked cycles,
versus 4,446,945 for the champion: an 8.16 percent throughput gain at equal
Fmax. Vendor Gowin placement options measured 67.091, 62.625 and 62.625 MHz.
The 62.625 MHz median gives 152.33 iterations/second, 5.97 percent above
the 143.74 champion and above the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Area was
4,814 logic cells, 1,804 registers, zero LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs.
These are isolated prototype measurements; implementation and the unchanged
evaluator must confirm them. The single mechanism is predictor-directed
lookahead, retaining the existing branch direction and target calculation.

The packed-vector prototype passed all 53 original single-retire ALTOPS
formal checks using unchanged wrapper/configuration/framework copies in
isolated temporary staging, including liveness and PC continuity. A
4,000-cycle independent deque-based cocotb model passed every occupancy,
ready/hold combination, simultaneous pop/refill, reset and correction.
Selftest and all three random programs passed full RVFI comparison with
and without instruction/data stalls. Canonical CoreMark passed all CRC,
UART, completion, bounded-access and timing-marker checks. Formal-deep
was not run; this proposal leaves M-extension arithmetic unchanged.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a four-entry fall-through fetched-instruction queue to if_stage, using
the current stateless aligned B/J predictor to advance a separate bus fetch
PC even while decode is blocked by load-use, data-memory or M-engine waits.
Capture each accepted response's own PC, instruction and exact
predicted_taken bit. When empty, supply the raw ready response directly to
decode. When occupied, supply only the registered head. Preserve empty
bypass: a registered-only refill stage fails the existing bounded liveness
check when an EX correction is followed by an eight-edge divide. No formal
depth, constraint or property may be changed to accommodate the queue.

Use four fixed flip-flop payload banks and a three-bit occupancy count.
Store explicit packed logic vectors, not an unpacked array of packed
structs: the current Yosys frontend misparses that structure-array
declaration as one-bit elements. A 66-bit vector represents the existing
if_id_t layout, including its valid and prediction bits; scalar struct
signals can represent the response and selected output. Do not add a RAM,
variable read pointer or new prediction table. Reset only occupancy and
bus PC; payload values are irrelevant when their slots are invalid.

Define pop as count!=0 && !stall_if && !redirect && !reset, empty bypass as
count==0 && !stall_if && !redirect && !reset, and bus acceptance as
io_imemReady && (count<4 || pop) && !redirect && !reset. An accepted empty
response consumed by bypass advances bus PC without entering the queue.
Every other accepted response is appended. On pop, shift remaining entries
toward the fixed head; append a simultaneous accepted response at the old
count-minus-pop position, with append priority over that bank's shift.
Increment or decrement occupancy only for enqueue without pop or pop
without enqueue. Full with pop allows replacement; full without pop holds
every bank and bus PC. Never consume data from an unready response.

Advance bus PC only on accepted acquisition, to predicted_target when the
captured prediction is taken and otherwise to PC+4. Queue-head validity is
count!=0; selected decode validity is count!=0 || io_imemReady. Wire that
selected validity, rather than raw bus readiness, to hazard_unit's
instruction-availability input. Keep if_stage's acquisition readiness on
actual io_imemReady. Thus an instruction-bus stall cannot block an available
queued head, while downstream holds and load-use still prevent decode
admission. Register-file addresses, decoder inputs and load-use comparisons
must all refer to the same selected instruction. Keep current registered
forwarding and validity-only ID/EX kill semantics.

An accepted EX correction has highest priority: clear occupancy, discard
any simultaneous response, kill the younger ID/EX capture, and set bus PC
to the existing resolved redirect target. Older data stalls defer correction
as today. Correct predictions neither flush nor bubble the queue. Carry
prediction from the consumed head; never recompute it from the advanced
bus PC. Preserve one-bit EX direct-control recovery, JALR resolution,
branch legality and target-alignment guards, resolved architectural RVFI
pc_wdata, nret=1 ports, retained WB bypass data, M-engine requests/results,
arithmetic and ALTOPS, traps, and exact-once memory effects and retirement.

Validate every occupancy from zero through four, empty bypass and capture,
simultaneous pop/enqueue, full holds, consumption while io_imemReady is
low, consecutive predicted B/J controls, loop exits and JALR corrections
with a full queue, reset, and correction overlapping load-use and data/M
waits. Use an independent queue model and architectural retirement checks.
Retain all existing assertions; adapt implementation observations that
equate speculative bus PC or raw bus readiness with blocked decode state
to observe the selected head and its availability instead. Do not relax
ID/EX hold, M latency, forwarding, order, trap or memory-effect assertions.
Run unchanged formal/cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC, UART, bounded-access
and timing-marker validation. Score all three Gowin placement options;
with 4,111,263 cycles the acceptance margin requires at least 61.814 MHz
median Fmax. The remaining risks are head-selection and queue-enable
routing, and formal proof complexity from the additional buffered state.

title: Four-bit parallel carry lookahead for base ALU arithmetic
motivation: The champion scores 165.86 iterations/sec at 73.757 MHz with 4,446,945 marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path is 20.005 ns through thirteen cells from ID/EX rs1 through EX/base ALU to dmem. Round 7 removed serial divider decisions, exposing ordinary forwarded address arithmetic. The prior round-2 micro_opt used eight-bit carry-select blocks inside four serial divider steps and regressed to 26.259 MHz; its launch/selection chain remained critical. Instead optimize only the single base-ALU addition or subtraction per instruction, using shorter four-bit blocks and parallel logarithmic carry prefix. Leave the now successful divider untouched.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the real base ALU ADD and SUB expressions with one reusable 32-bit modulo adder function made from eight parallel four-bit blocks, a balanced three-level block carry-prefix network, and local carry-select result muxes. ADD invokes it with x=a,y=b,cin=0; SUB invokes it with x=a,y=~b,cin=1. Do not share their operation-controlled operand inversion ahead of ADD, since loads/stores always use ADD and should not acquire another late control mux. Keep all ALU encodings, combinational interfaces and instruction latencies unchanged.

For block k compute two independent exact five-bit sums S0[k]={0,x[4k+:4]}+{0,y[4k+:4]} and S1[k]={0,x[4k+:4]}+{0,y[4k+:4]}+1. These are parallel short native carry chains, never sums of previously selected blocks. Set G[k]=S0[k][4] and P[k]=&(S0[k][3:0]). P from the low sum is correct: when those four bits are all ones, carry-in can carry through the block; if G is already one its value dominates regardless of P. Fold cin into G[0] as G[0]|(P[0]&cin).

Build explicit prefix levels at strides 1,2,4. At each level and each k at least the stride, combine only the previous level: G_next[k]=G_prev[k]|(P_prev[k]&G_prev[k-stride]), P_next[k]=P_prev[k]&P_prev[k-stride]; otherwise copy that group. Carry into block zero is cin, and carry into block k>0 is the final prefix G[k-1]. Select S1[k][3:0] or S0[k][3:0] with that carry. Discard final carry, retaining exact 32-bit wraparound. Do not introduce a serial eight-block carry recurrence, a full-width increment after a chosen sum, or a second full-width ripple adder in parallel.

This changes only the combinational base ADD/SUB implementation. Preserve every existing multiply/divide expression and ALTOPS formula, both M-engine handshakes and latencies, launch operand capture, forwarding, branch arithmetic, PC arithmetic, decode legality, stage payloads, stalls, traps and nret=1 IO. In particular do not apply this helper to the divider or change its radix-16 prefix/recurrence. The desired gain is shorter carry propagation on the observed ALU/address path at identical marked cycles; increased LUTs, local mux delay and newly limiting divider/redirect paths are risks.

Prove the helper equals (x+y+cin) modulo 2^32 for arbitrary operands and both carry inputs using a local combinational SAT property without touching the shared formal wrapper/configuration. Add independent ADD/SUB references with seeded random values and directed carry propagation through consecutive all-ones four-bit block sums, carry-generate/kill patterns at every nibble boundary, borrow across bit 31 and unsigned wraparound. Retain all existing arithmetic and pipeline assertions. Run the unchanged single-retire formal checks, stalled/unstalled full-trace cosim and canonical stalled CoreMark with all CRC/UART/bounds/marker gates. Expect exactly 4,446,945 marked cycles; acceptance at unchanged cycles needs median vendor Fmax above 77.150 MHz. Measure all three Gowin placement options. The expected gain is a timing hypothesis, not a claim that the acceptance gate has already passed.

title: Partition execute into fast address and late multiply paths
motivation:
Registered M operands improved timing, but the champion's two-edge
multiplier blocks EX even for independent following instructions.
The r6 structural change increased marked CoreMark cycles by 4.40%,
from 4,259,699 to 4,446,945, while separating the multiplier from live
bypasses. The champion reaches 73.757 MHz and 165.86 iterations/sec.
Its worst path runs through ordinary EX/ALU execution toward dmem.
Mapping multiplication onto existing EX/MEM operand and MEM/WB result
boundaries can preserve registered DSP inputs while removing multiply
results from the EX mux and multiplication from blocking-M control.
Separate load/store addressing is the fast half of this partition:
memory requests need only forwarded rs1+imm, yet their addresses
currently traverse the general ALU operation and link-result muxes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU ordinary pipelined instructions that
execute their arithmetic in MEM instead of holding EX. At the normal
EX/MEM edge capture forwarded architectural rs1, rs2, operation and
instruction metadata. Compute the selected product only from those
registered operands during MEM and capture its final 32-bit value
directly into the existing MEM/WB selected writeback register.
These two existing edges provide operand and result capture; add no
pipeline stage and never send live EX bypasses through a multiplier.
Independent instructions and successive independent multiplies may
advance every cycle. Keep one in-order retirement on RVFI channel 0
at the normal MEM/WB boundary.

Partition the existing EX/MEM boundary into independent architectural
result and LSU effective-address channels. Add a 32-bit effective_addr
field, captured directly from forwarded rs1+imm with a dedicated adder.
Route dmem_addr, alignment checks, lane position, load extraction and
RVFI aligned memory address from this channel exclusively. Do not route
it through ALU operand-source, operation-result, multiply or link muxes.
General ALU/link results remain authoritative for ordinary writeback
and EX/MEM forwarding. Loads select their data before MEM/WB as before.
Preserve full-width wrapping address arithmetic, byte/halfword/word
semantics, reset, true memory holds and exact payload/control association.
Neither half of this execute partition adds a pipeline stage.

Remove multiply launch/busy/sticky-result/consume from core execution
control; leave the eight-edge blocking divider unchanged. The normal
EX result path must no longer select a multiplier product. Preserve
separate signed-signed, unsigned-unsigned and signed-unsigned product
semantics and the established Gowin DSP inference unless an equivalent
mapping is verified. MUL uses the low unsigned product; MULH, MULHU
and MULHSU select their correct high halves. Preserve every ALTOPS
constant and raw-operand formula in the MEM multiply datapath.

A multiply result becomes forwardable from MEM/WB, not EX/MEM.
Treat valid EX multiplies as late-result producers with the existing
load-use replay rule for an immediately following consumer: hold fetch,
inject one invalid ID/EX slot, let the multiply advance, then replay
its dependent with the registered MEM/WB bypass selection. Never use
the EX/MEM placeholder as an architectural multiply bypass. Preserve
youngest-writer priority, x0, same-cycle RF writes and retained WB
data when valid clears during a memory hold. Test both source positions,
stores, branches, JALR, loads, further multiplies and divider launch.
Distinguish actual multiply consumers from register-field aliases in
immediate, upper-immediate, direct-jump and other source-free encodings.
Source-aware replay may suppress a multiply-use bubble only when the
corresponding architectural operand is unused. Preserve conservative
load-use behavior. RVFI still reports both raw register fields: if an
unused field aliases the multiply in MEM, capture that product into
the instruction's RVFI rs1_val or rs2_val rather than its EX placeholder.
This late correction must feed verification metadata only. Add separate
EX/MEM multiply operand fields captured from ordinary forwarded rs1/rs2,
and use those for the physical MEM multiplier. Do not feed the late
product through a functional EX operand, address adder, branch comparator,
store-data path or a subsequent multiplier operand register. This avoids
creating a timed DSP-to-EX feedback path while retaining exact RVFI data.

Retain genuine dmem backpressure: hold pending EX/MEM instructions and
operands, prevent younger EX acceptance, and clear only WB valid while
retaining its forwarding payload. Multiplication has no memory request.
A not-ready dmem bus must not stall a MEM multiply in the absence of an
actual unaccepted memory request. Preserve reset, squash, redirect,
exact-once stores and retirement priorities. Divider waits must drain
an older MEM multiply exactly once and retain divider launch operands
after their bypass sources advance.

Keep nret=1 and every top-level port, trap and decoder legality check,
formal depth, eight-edge divide deadline and ten-clock branch-to-divide
bound unchanged. Retain arithmetic vectors and architectural pipeline
assertions. Adapt multiplier-only internal blocking-state expectations
to the new two-stage product path, one-bubble dependent replay,
independent one-per-cycle advancement, stalled operand preservation
and exact-once retirement. Check the physical multiplier against
independent RV32M arithmetic, including signed high halves and random
operands. Run unchanged formal and full-RVFI cosim plus canonical
stalled CoreMark CRC, UART, bounds and marker checks. Measure all three
Gowin placements. The principal risks are DSP-to-MEM/WB selection timing
and the frequency of immediate multiply dependencies. Acceptance

title: Prediction-guided fetch queue with validity-only recovery
motivation:
The current champion has cheap backward-taken/JAL prediction and registered
M-extension engines, but instruction acquisition still stops whenever
decode waits for a load, data memory, or an M-extension result. Ready
instruction-bus cycles during these holds are discarded, and subsequent
instruction stalls delay admission again. Existing branch prediction can
guide useful fetch work during those execution holds without adding a
direction table or a wide target cache.

Predictor history supports this choice. Bimodal and exception predictors
saved only about one additional percent of cycles relative to the static
predictor and sacrificed clock frequency. The r7s2 four-entry lookahead
candidate used 4,111,263 marked CoreMark cycles versus its parent's
4,446,945, an 8.16 percent throughput improvement at equal Fmax. It scored
161.29 iterations/second at 66.311 MHz, but retained the older divider and
lost to r7s0's parallel prefix/recurrence improvement. The current r7s0
champion retains 4,446,945 cycles and raises median Fmax to 73.757 MHz.
Apply only predictor-guided lookahead to this newer champion; preserving
its registered radix-16 arithmetic directly addresses that prior loss.

A fresh isolated prototype on the supplied champion reproduced 4,111,263
marked cycles. Gating every queue payload write with EX correction gave
only 69.688 MHz median Fmax and failed the acceptance margin. Separating
payload storage from occupancy/PC reset and correction instead measured
75.093, 75.023 and 75.023 MHz in the three Gowin placement options. The
75.023 MHz median yields 182.48 iterations/second, 10.02 percent above
165.86. Area was 5,865 logic cells, 2,038 registers, zero LUT RAMs, four
BSRAMs and six DSPs. These are isolated prototype measurements, requiring
confirmation by implementation and the unchanged evaluator. Canonical
stalled CoreMark passed every CRC, UART, bounded-access and marker check.
Selftest and all three random programs passed complete RVFI comparisons
both with and without bus stalls. A 5,000-cycle independent deque model
passed all occupancies, reset/correction, ready/hold combinations, empty
bypass, unready consumption, full holds and simultaneous pop/refill.
The final prototype also passed lint and all 53 original single-retire
ALTOPS formal checks in isolated staging using unchanged wrappers,
configuration, proof depths and framework sources. Arithmetic RTL was
unchanged; formal-deep was not run.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one four-entry fall-through fetched-instruction queue in if_stage.
Keep the current stateless aligned backward-taken/forward-not-taken and
always-taken JAL predictor. Look it up using the bus fetch PC and raw
response, then advance a separate fetch PC on every accepted acquisition,
even while decode is blocked by load-use, data-memory, or M-engine waits.
Each queued payload holds its own PC, instruction, and the exact
predicted_taken bit used for that acquisition. This is a single
predictor-guided lookahead mechanism, with no new predictor training.

Implement four fixed 66-bit packed-vector flip-flop banks, a three-bit
occupancy count, and a fixed queue head. Avoid an unpacked array of packed
structs, which previously confused the formal Verilog frontend; scalar
if_id_t views can wrap the packed payloads. Reset occupancy and bus PC;
invalid payloads need no reset. When empty, bypass a ready raw response
directly to decode, retaining today's no-extra-stage fetch latency and
bounded liveness. When occupied, decode reads the registered head.
Decode availability is count!=0 || io_imemReady. Route this availability
to the hazard unit's imem_ready input, while acquisition continues to use
the actual io_imemReady signal. All decode, RF-address, forwarding-match,
and load-use logic must see the same selected instruction.

Separate speculative payload movement from architectural acceptance.
Compute storage_pop = count!=0 && !stall_if, storage_accept =
io_imemReady && (count<4 || storage_pop), storage_bypass = count==0 &&
!stall_if, and storage_enqueue = storage_accept && !storage_bypass.
Append at count-minus-storage_pop; shift remaining banks toward the head
on storage_pop, with append taking priority at its destination. Put all
payload-bank updates in their own always_ff block with NO reset or
redirect qualification on its enables or data selects. Writes/shifts on
a reset/correction edge are allowed because the independently flushed
occupancy makes those values unreachable. This removes EX comparator/
forwarded-operand recovery paths from the wide queue's write controls.
Reset and correction must still suppress architectural acquisition and
admission; speculative bank writes do not constitute admitted fetches.

In a separate PC/occupancy always_ff block, reset has highest priority,
accepted EX correction is next, and normal storage_accept/pop/enqueue
controls apply only in the remaining case. Thus a response bypassed and
consumed while empty does not enqueue. A full queue permits simultaneous
pop/refill but holds bus PC and payloads when it cannot pop. Empty with a
decode hold can acquire into the queue. Increment occupancy only for
enqueue without pop; decrement only for pop without enqueue. Outside
reset/correction, advance bus PC only on storage_accept, to the captured
prediction's target or fetch PC+4. Never capture an unready response,
advance for a discarded response, or admit a queued instruction twice.

An accepted EX correction takes priority over acquisition and admission:
clear occupancy, discard any same-cycle response architecturally, squash
the younger decode capture, and set bus PC to the existing resolved
redirect_target. Do not reintroduce correction into payload-bank enables.
Older data stalls defer correction exactly as today. Correctly predicted
direct controls preserve the queue; loop exits, JALRs and mispredictions
discard its entire wrong path. Carry the consumed head's prediction
through ID/EX, never a fresh lookup at the advanced bus PC. Preserve
one-bit direct-control recovery, JALR resolution, legality and alignment
guards, resolved RVFI next PC, contiguous exact-once retirement, and
suppression of wrong-path memory effects.

Base implementation on the supplied current champion, retaining its
registered forwarding selectors, selected MEM/WB result, sticky M-engine
completion, two-edge multiply, eight-edge divider, parallel narrow-prefix
and full-width radix-16 trials, and ALTOPS behavior. Keep nret=1 and every
top-level port. No arithmetic, decoder, memory-access semantics, formal
assumptions, proof depths, evaluation tools or benchmark files change.

Validate the queue against an independent deque model across occupancies
zero through four, empty bypass/capture, simultaneous pop/refill, full
holds, queued consumption with an unready bus, consecutive predicted
controls, reset, and correction at every occupancy. Pipeline tests must
combine loop exits/JALR corrections with load-use, data and M-engine
holds and check RVFI PCs/order, forwarding operands, and exact-once memory
effects. Preserve existing architectural assertions; update observations
that previously equated speculative bus PC with the decoded PC to check
the selected decode head and actual admission instead. Run unchanged
lint, unit tests, formal and cosim, canonical CRC/UART/OOB/marker checks,
and all three Gowin placement options.

The isolated final prototype predicts 182.48 iterations/second and a
10.02 percent gain. Beating 165.86 by 4.6 percent requires approximately
71.33 MHz median Fmax at 4,111,263 cycles. Queue head selection and enable
routing remain material risks; retaining the specified payload/control
separation is essential because the fully gated prototype did not meet
that threshold. The orchestrator must confirm these prototype results.

title: Bypass the general ALU for registered effective addresses
motivation:
The champion scores 179.84 iterations/second at 73.936 MHz with
4,111,263 marked CoreMark cycles. Data-memory address currently
comes from the general ALU result, including operand substitutions,
ALU operation selection and jump-link selection. The r8s1 history
separated addresses alongside a much larger late-multiply change.
Isolate address specialization on today's fetch-queue champion.
The address specialization removes general ALU selection from an
externally timed path without adding an execution stage or changing
CoreMark's instruction throughput.

title: Partition execute into early LSU and pipelined MEM multiply channels
motivation:
The champion's fetch queue hides instruction stalls, but multiplication
still blocks EX for operand capture and product capture. EX/MEM and
MEM/WB can supply those two register boundaries while independent
instructions continue. A separate LSU address channel keeps general
arithmetic result selection out of the timed memory-address path.

Structural r8s1 established this partition on the earlier champion:

improvement. It lost to the fetch-queue candidate rather than failing
correctness. Apply this topology to the supplied fetch-queue champion;
measure its benefit under actual stalls because the queue already
overlaps instruction acquisition with blocking multiplication.

An isolated prototype on the supplied RTL measured Gowin options 0/1/2

zero LUT RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs. Canonical CoreMark CRCs,
validation text, bounded accesses and timing markers passed. Selftest
and all three random programs passed full RVFI comparison with both
ready-high and stalled buses. All 53 original single-retire ALTOPS formal
checks passed in private staging with unchanged wrappers, configuration,
depths and framework sources. Formal-deep was not run. These are
prototype measurements requiring reproduction by implementation and
the unchanged evaluator.

Repartition the existing EX/MEM boundary into an early LSU address
channel and a late multiply operand channel. Execute MUL/MULH/MULHU/
MULHSU in MEM, using EX/MEM for forwarded operand capture and MEM/WB
for product capture. This is one structural execution partition across
existing stages: add no pipeline stage, retain one in-order retirement
on channel 0, and preserve the fetch queue and eight-edge divider.

Add effective_addr and dedicated multiply_a/multiply_b fields to EX/MEM,
preferably at its MSB to preserve existing packed-field offsets.
Capture effective_addr directly from forwarded rs1+imm with a dedicated
full-width wrapping adder on normal EX acceptance. Use it exclusively
for dmem_addr, alignment checks, lane masks, load extraction and aligned
RVFI memory address. Preserve original ALU/link writeback and EX/MEM
forwarding. No product, divider result or general ALU result mux may
precede the LSU address register; avoid opcode-dependent wide enables.

Multiply advances normally into MEM without launch/busy/completion
waits. Capture both functional forwarded operands and operation with
the instruction. Compute the product exclusively from those registers,
selecting it before MEM/WB capture alongside load and ALU/link data.
Preserve the established widened signed-signed, unsigned-unsigned and
signed-unsigned expressions and six-DSP mapping. MUL takes the unsigned
low half; all high-half variants retain exact RV32M signedness. Preserve
every ALTOPS raw-operand formula and constant in the physical multiplier.

Remove multiply waiting from core control; divider_wait represents
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU only. The standalone alu may retain its tested multiply
request interface: tie both multiply controls inactive in EX so unused
arithmetic is pruned. The prototype used this arrangement with six DSPs
total. Remove obsolete EX control and unused wires without weakening
lint. Preserve divider launch operands, sticky completion, exact
eight-edge latency, sign correction and all arithmetic corner cases.

Multiply becomes functionally forwardable from MEM/WB. Extend existing
load-use replay to valid legal EX multiplies with a nonzero destination
actually consumed by the next decode instruction: hold consumption,
inject one invalid ID/EX slot, advance the multiply and replay through
registered MEM/WB forwarding. Independent instructions and independent
consecutive multiplies advance every cycle. Decode actual opcode source
usage to exclude unused aliases from multiply replay; retain the
existing conservative load-use rule. Preserve youngest-writer priority,
x0, same-cycle RF write-through and retained WB forwarding under stalls.

RVFI still reports raw register fields for source-free and immediate
instructions. If an unused field matches a multiply in MEM through an
EX/MEM forwarding selector, correct only captured RVFI rs1_val/rs2_val
with the MEM product. This correction feeds verification metadata
exclusively. The physical multiplier uses separate functional operand
registers captured before correction. Never feed corrected metadata
into ALU/address operands, branch comparison, store data or subsequent
multiplier operands. True consumers replay through MEM/WB, including
stores, branches, JALR, address bases and other M operations.

Hold all new EX/MEM fields under genuine memory backpressure. A MEM
multiply generates no bus request and does not stall merely because
io_dmemReady is low. Pending loads/stores retain payload until acceptance;
clear only WB valid while retaining forwarding data. Divider waits
drain an older multiply once. Preserve reset cancellation, redirect
squash, illegal/wrong-path side-effect suppression, exact-once stores,
contiguous retirement, nret=1, every port and the ten-clock ready-high
branch-to-divide bound. Change no decoder, wrapper, proof depth,
benchmark, memory contract or evaluation file.

Retain every arithmetic expected value and architectural assertion.
Replace observations of old multiply launch/consume phases with normal
EX/MEM acceptance, MEM/WB completion, one-bubble replay, held payloads,
reset cancellation and exact-once retirement. The prototype passed
34 of 39 original pipeline tests; the remaining five stopped on old
blocking-multiply observations and require these explicit replacements,
while retaining their architectural checks. Include the new source in
applicable tests. Check the physical multiplier against every existing
MUL vector plus seeded signed/unsigned references. Exercise unused
aliases, both bypasses, consecutive multiplies, mixed M/LSU chains,
reset, wrong paths and both bus-stall modes.

title: Hashed static-agreement prediction from registered branch results
motivation:
The champion uses backward-taken/forward-not-taken direction prediction and a
four-entry prediction-guided queue. Previous bimodal and tagged exception
predictors reduced cycles but lost FPGA timing. An agreement predictor learns
whether to keep or invert each instruction's own static bias, so oppositely
biased branches can share counters constructively. A small PC-folded table
needs no tags, target RAM, valid bitmap or speculative history.

An isolated 32-entry prototype with PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7] indexing, fixed FF
counters, Boolean saturating transitions and training from registered EX/MEM
metadata measured 4,030,475 canonical marked cycles versus 4,111,263 for the
champion, a 2.004 percent throughput gain. Gowin placement options measured
75.164, 73.966 and 73.966 MHz: median 73.966 MHz and fitness 183.517 iter/sec,
a 2.045 percent gain over 179.84. It passed lint, all canonical CRC/UART/OOB/
marker checks and eight complete selftest/random RVFI trace comparisons with
and without bus stalls. The counter transition truth table matches independent
saturating integer arithmetic for every state and both outcomes. Formal and
full cocotb gates remain for implementation; arithmetic was untouched.

These prototype results do not yet meet the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
At the measured cycles qualification requires median Fmax above 75.817 MHz.
The single proposed mechanism is compact static-agreement prediction; its
remaining risk is physical routing and the cost of lookup/update state.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Extend the current direct-control predictor with one 32-entry static-
agreement table indexed by PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7]. Each two-bit saturating counter records
agreement with BTFNT: reset to 3, increment when actual direction matches
instruction bit 31, and decrement on disagreement. For a legal aligned
conditional branch predict instr[31] XOR !counter[1]. Retain aligned JAL
always taken and JALR sequential. Preserve the existing 30-bit B/J target
addition and legality/alignment guards. Aliases affect accuracy only because
direct targets always come from the actual fetched instruction.

Use 32 fixed two-bit flip-flop words with independent decoded enables;
reset the 64 bits to strong agreement. No tags, valid bitmap, target storage,
history, pending-event queue or RAM is required. Read only disagreement from
the counter MSBs, with constant-index address selects and a balanced OR tree.
For old high/low counter bits h,l and registered agreement a, implement exact
saturating next state as h_next=(h&l)|(a&(h|l)) and
l_next=(h&~l)|(a&(h|~l)). Each next bit is a three-input Boolean function,
avoiding general add/subtract and saturation selection networks.

Train directly from the existing registered EX/MEM branch metadata, rather
than adding live EX resolution inputs or another update register. At its
outgoing MEM acceptance edge, use ex_mem_w.pc for the update index and
ex_mem_w.branch_taken == ex_mem_w.instr[31] for agreement. Update once when
ex_mem_w.valid && !reset && !hold_mem_wb && ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_branch &&
!ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_illegal && ex_mem_w.pc[1:0]==0 && !ex_mem_w.instr[8].
The branch has already survived EX validity, trap and downstream hold checks;
these register outputs isolate predictor feedback from live forwarded branch
operands. Do not introduce an EX arithmetic or comparison operation for
training. A held EX branch generates no repeated table updates, reset cancels
updates, and adjacent accepted branches update in order even at the same
index. Exclude misaligned direct targets conservatively even when not taken.

Preserve the exact prediction already captured with every accepted fetch in
the queue and ID/EX. EX compares that captured bit with resolved effective
direction; never reconstruct it from the current counter. Retain one-bit
correction and its priority, occupancy-only queue recovery, all payload

title: Thermometer-guided balanced muxes for divider remainders
motivation:
The r9s1 champion scores 191.26 iterations/sec at 77.500 MHz and
4,052,037 marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst vendor path is inside
divider prefix initialization: captured divisor bit 1 to remainder
bit 7, 19.241 ns through 22 cells. The r7s0 micro_opt succeeded by
fusing both narrow and wide trial banks; selecting their results is
now a remaining cost. Current selection computes adjacent-fit one-hot
bits, masks sixteen data candidates and reduces them through four OR
levels. Ordered unsigned multiples already make the fit vector a
thermometer code, permitting a shorter selection network without any
arithmetic, register, pipeline or instruction-latency change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the one-hot masked-OR remainder/digit selection in both
the edge-two prefix and full-width radix-16 recurrence with a balanced
sixteen-leaf mux tree controlled directly by existing trial-fit bits.
Preserve every subtractor, exact multiple width, Boolean nibble lookup,
normalization, register, eight-edge completion and ALTOPS expression.
This is one local arithmetic-result selection optimization.

The current exact trials produce fit[k]=(T>=kD), with fit[0]=1 and
fit[16]=0. For D>0 the fitting candidates form a contiguous prefix;
for D=0 every candidate 0..15 fits. Thus the largest fitting candidate
can be chosen by binary partitioning without an adjacent-fit decoder.
Keep candidate 0's remainder as T, and candidates 1..15 as the low
8-bit prefix or 32-bit recurrence subtraction result, respectively.
Each leaf also carries its constant four-bit digit index.

For pair k, select leaf 2k+1 when fit[2k+1] is true, otherwise leaf 2k.
For quad k, select the higher pair when fit[4k+2] is true. For oct k,
select the higher quad when fit[8k+4] is true. Select the higher oct
when fit[8] is true. Apply the identical selectors to remainder and
digit at every level. All fit predicates are computed in parallel
by the unchanged trial bank: this is four levels of ordinary two-way
muxing, not four serial compare/subtract decisions. Express balanced
fixed-index wiring explicitly so no priority chain or indexed RAM is
inferred. Native Gowin mux resources may absorb successive levels.

Remove the old candidate-data masks and OR reductions. Retain or
re-express the adjacent-fit one-hot signals solely as verification
monitors for the existing one-hot/monotonic-fit properties; they must
not gate functional remainder or quotient data. Preserve the prefix's
final D>=256 quotient/remainder override, nibble high-divisor guard,
full 12/13-bit prefix multiple/subtract widths and full 36/37-bit
recurrence widths. D=0 must select leaf 15 and retain T, equality with
kD must choose k, and T<D must choose zero. No multiple truncation,
limb comparator, carry-select adder or initialization retiming is
part of the delivered hypothesis.

Keep launch/consume, captured operands, sticky result, reset,
signed normalization/correction, INT_MIN/-1, divide-by-zero, RVFI,
nret=1, traps, memory backpressure, forwarding, multiplication and
fetch behavior unchanged. Preserve every decoder legality and every
architectural assertion. All changes stay in bench RTL/unit tests.

Prove mux selection equivalent to the former masked-OR selection for
all monotonic fit patterns and arbitrary candidate payloads, including
all-fit zero division. Retain all existing real-arithmetic prefix
identity/equivalence, exact multiple, recurrence, one-hot and fit-order
properties without weakening constraints. Retain arithmetic vectors
and per-edge state/handshake assertions. Add directed selected-digit
boundaries kD-1,kD,kD+1 for every k, equality, zero divisors and high-bit
multiples; check complete signed/unsigned DIV/REM results independently.
Run unchanged single-retire formal, full-RVFI stalled/unstalled cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/markers and all vendor placements.

Expect unchanged 4,052,037 marked cycles and higher Fmax by removing
adjacent-fit gating plus a data-mask level ahead of the reduction.
Acceptance needs median Fmax above about 81.066 MHz. Mux-tree routing,
control fanout, serial prefix arithmetic and EX redirect may become
limits; vendor timing is required before asserting acceptance.

title: Consume store data in MEM through a dedicated late bypass
motivation:
The champion reaches 191.26 iterations/sec at 77.5 MHz and 4,052,037
marked CoreMark cycles. Its early LSU address and MEM multiply channels
improve overlap, but stores still consume both operands in EX. Only
the address base is needed there. A store following the load or
multiply producing its data unnecessarily replays even though the
final value reaches MEM/WB when that store reaches MEM.
Previous structural execution partitioning succeeded in r9s1.
Local divider-retiming probes achieved only 71.483 to 75.320 MHz
median; their changes are excluded from this proposal.
