hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move store rs2 consumption from EX to MEM with a dedicated MEM/WB-to-MEM
store-data bypass. Remove only immediate load/multiply replay caused
exclusively by a store's data operand. Keep its address-base dependency
in EX. This is one structural operand-consumption change across existing
stages. Preserve the pipeline, fetch queue, early LSU address, MEM
multiply, eight-edge divider, nret=1 and other instruction latencies.

Classify STORE instructions for hazard handling. Exclude their rs2
match from immediate load/multiply hazards, but retain replay for rs1,
including rs1==rs2. Preserve existing non-store source rules, conservative
non-store load-use handling, validity, legality, x0 and downstream
hold/redirect/divider priorities. A late producer followed by a store
using only its result as data should advance without a replay bubble.

Preserve an architectural fallback in EX/MEM.write_data. At the decode
forwarding-selector edge, a STORE must not select an immediately
preceding EX load or multiply as its rs2 EX/MEM source: alu_result is
not that producer's completed value. Instead select the next eligible
older MEM producer, then the write-first RF value. Keep ordinary rs1,
non-store and mature-ALU forwarding. This fallback is essential when
a preceding misaligned load later suppresses its write: the store
then needs the previous architectural value, including an older writer
still in the pipeline. Merely removing replay while capturing the
unready EX/MEM placeholder is incorrect.

In MEM, select MEM/WB's final value when retained write eligibility is
true and its nonzero destination matches the store rs2 address; otherwise
use the captured fallback. Select before SB/SH/SW byte replication.
Use captured alignment-checked MEM/WB control eligibility, rather than
wb_w_en or retirement valid: memory stalls clear valid while retaining
the older value and bypass eligibility. A stalled store must retain
correct request data until accepted exactly once. Preserve youngest
writer priority, x0, trapped producer suppression, widths, masks and
alignment traps.

Capture the selected unreplicated store value as RVFI rs2_rdata and its
replicated value as RVFI mem_wdata. Preserve raw RVFI fields for other
instructions, contiguous retirement and trap discipline. The bypass
feeds only store data and associated metadata. It must not feed LSU
addresses, branch resolution, multiplier operands or general EX ALU
operands. Change no arithmetic, predictor, wrapper, proof depth,
benchmark source or evaluation contract.

Retain all existing assertions. Add LW/LB/LH and all MUL-variant store
chains, SB/SH/SW lanes, zero data-only replay, same-register base/data
dependencies that still replay, youngest-writer priority, older-writer
plus misaligned-load fallback, x0, wrong paths and reset. Verify complete
RVFI operands/results/memory fields, retained forwarding, stable stalled
requests and exact-once effects under both bus-stall modes. Keep the
ten-clock ready-high branch-to-divide check and every decoder check.

Run unchanged lint, units, single-retire ALTOPS formal, full-RVFI
selftest/random cosim, canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/marker validation
and all three Gowin placements. Removing dependency bubbles must
outweigh the new store-data mux and tag fanout. Divider initialization
and branch recovery may still limit frequency. Require measured fitness
above 200.058 iterations/sec, the champion plus 4.6 percent.

title: Cached local-history direction prediction with parallel bank training
motivation:
The champion uses static backward-taken/forward-not-taken prediction and a
four-entry predicted-path queue. The prior 32-entry agreement predictor saved
about 2 percent in marked cycles but lost FPGA timing. A serial history-table
and pattern-table lookup risks repeating that failure. Precomputing each
bank's next agreement bit moves history-dependent work onto the registered
training path and gives fetch only a shallow one-bit lookup.

A canonical ten-iteration reference trace counted 111,175 static conditional
direction misses. An immediate-update model of 64 independent banks, each
with two local-history bits and four two-bit agreement counters, counted
40,412 misses, versus 47,235 for the prior 32-entry agreement table. This is
an architectural trace estimate, not a stalled RTL or FPGA measurement;
queue lookahead and delayed training can reduce the gain. The expected cycle
benefit alone is below the acceptance margin, so the cached lookup must also
preserve or improve placement timing. At unchanged cycles qualification
requires more than 81.065 MHz; a 2.2 percent cycle reduction lowers that
requirement to approximately 79.28 MHz.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only conditional direction selection with one cached local-history
predictor. Use 64 banks indexed by PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8]. Each bank holds a
two-bit resolved direction history H, four two-bit saturating agreement
counters C[0..3], and one cached agreement bit A. Reset H to zero, all C to
strong agreement (3), and A to one. For a legal aligned conditional branch
predict instr[31] XOR !A[fetch_index]. Keep the existing aligned B/J target
addition, JAL always taken, JALR sequential, and legality/alignment guards.
No history or pattern lookup may be placed between fetch PC and prediction:
fetch reads only the 64 cached bits through decoded selects and a balanced
OR tree. This is one local-history mechanism, without a BTB or target cache.

Train from registered EX/MEM metadata exactly once when ex_mem_w.valid &&
!reset && !hold_mem_wb && ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_branch &&
!ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_illegal && ex_mem_w.pc[1:0]==0 && !ex_mem_w.instr[8].
For the update bank compute agreement G=(branch_taken==instr[31]), update
only C[H] with saturation toward G, and shift the actual direction into
Hnext={H[0],branch_taken}. On that same edge cache Cnext[Hnext][1]. If Hnext
equals old H, bypass the newly updated counter MSB; otherwise select the
existing counter at Hnext. This forwarding is required for repeated all-zero
and all-one histories. Preserve other banks and patterns. Adjacent accepted
updates to one bank must observe the preceding edge's new state.

Implement every bank and pattern with fixed flip-flop words and independent
decoded enables: 128 history bits, 512 counter bits and 64 cached bits, for
704 predictor state bits. Use constant-index masked reads inside each bank
so neither history nor pattern state infers RAM. For old counter bits h,l,
the exact saturating next bits are hnext=(h&l)|(G&(h|l)) and
lnext=(h&~l)|(G&(h|~l)). Every bank's next-context selection is local and
parallel; avoid a global multiplexed history read followed by a global
counter read. All training inputs are registered branch metadata, not live
forwarded EX operands, redirect or instruction-bus acceptance.

Resolved history is deliberately nonspeculative. No history rollback or
extra queue metadata is needed. EX must compare the actual direction with
the exact predicted_taken already captured with each accepted fetch, never
recompute its prediction from current state. Delayed updates and aliases
affect accuracy only. Preserve occupancy-only queue recovery, validity-only
kills, accepted correction priority, bus handshakes, forwarding, load-use
and multiply replay, M arithmetic/ALTOPS, decoder legality, alignment traps,
nret=1 ports, resolved architectural RVFI next PC and contiguous retirement.

Verify all counter states against independent saturating integer arithmetic,
every history transition, same-context bypass, unchanged future-context
selection, same-bank aliases, consecutive registered updates, no update on
holds, reset, and cold static behavior. Retain exhaustive B/J target and
reserved-encoding checks. Pipeline cases must combine changing predictor
state with queued instructions, loop exits, forward branches, every existing
hold reason and wrong-path stores, checking full RVFI PCs, operands, order
and exact-once memory effects. Run unchanged lint, formal and cosim gates,
canonical bracketed CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB validation and all three Gowin
placement options. Qualification requires fitness above 200.058 iter/sec;
increased FF placement density and cached-update routing are the main risks.

title: Precompute PC-derived recovery addresses at decode
motivation:
The r10s0 champion reaches 203.70 iterations/sec at 82.542 MHz with
4,052,037 marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst vendor path now runs from
ID/EX rs1 bit 2 through EX to the fetch PC, 17.588 ns through 39 cells.
Earlier divider and address optimizations removed their serial result
selection costs; branch recovery is the next exposed timing limit.
Recovery mixes PC-derived target arithmetic with late branch resolution.
A target-preselection-only prototype measured 83.617 MHz median, a
1.30 percent gain that falls short of acceptance. Retiming PC-derived
address arithmetic into the existing decode edge is a focused refinement.

they do not need forwarded EX operands or branch direction. This is

title: Isolate branch recovery with speculative fetch and decode state
motivation:
The champion scores 203.70 iterations/sec at 82.542 MHz with 4,052,037
marked CoreMark cycles. After the balanced divider-selector improvement,
its worst vendor path is ID/EX.rs1_val bit 2 through EX to IF.pc bit 9,
17.588 ns through 39 cells. The r8s1 and r10s1 structural experiments
also ended on forwarded-operand-to-fetch-PC paths. Recent store-data
retiming saved only 0.02 percent of cycles, while successful r3s1 and
r8s2 changes isolated wide payload storage from late squash/recovery
control. Apply that separation to the fetch address itself. Simply
delaying redirect would add recovery bubbles and threaten the unchanged
ten-clock ready-high branch-to-divide successor-retirement bound.

marked CoreMark cycles. After the balanced divider-selector improvement,
its worst vendor path is ID/EX.rs1_val bit 2 through EX to IF.pc bit 9,
17.588 ns through 39 cells. The r8s1 and r10s1 structural experiments
also ended on forwarded-operand-to-fetch-PC paths. Recent store-data
retiming saved only 0.02 percent of cycles, while successful r3s1 and
r8s2 changes isolated wide payload storage from late squash/recovery
control. Apply that separation to the fetch address itself. Simply

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure fetch state around parallel next, held and recovery address
banks and speculative occupancy, with a small registered selection token.
Capture candidate recovery
addresses on the very edge that currently updates the PC on redirect;
select the captured bank immediately after that edge. This separates
forwarded target arithmetic from branch comparison, alignment checking
and redirect qualification without adding a recovery cycle. It is one
structural change to fetch/decode recovery-state storage, retaining
the predictor, four-entry fetch queue and all execution latencies.

In EX expose two unqualified address candidates: resolved_target is
JALR's wrapping rs1+imm with bit zero cleared for JALR, otherwise pc+imm;
fallthrough_target is wrapping pc+4. The resolved-target data selection
depends only on the decoded JALR bit, never branch_cond, direct_taken,
misalign_fault, divider completion, reset or downstream acceptance.
Expose the existing predicted_taken&&!direct_taken decision as a
correction-kind bit, used only when the existing qualified redirect
event is true. Preserve the exact existing branch/jump alignment traps,
reg_write suppression and next-PC/RVFI behavior. Keep the existing
selected redirect_target available for verification if useful, but
disconnect it from functional fetch-address storage.

In IF add resolved_target_q and fallthrough_target_q, both sampled on
every clock edge with no reset, hold, redirect or request-valid gates.
They cannot be selected until a valid accepted correction captures a
corresponding token on that same edge. Use a registered token with
NEXT, HELD, RESOLVED and FALLTHROUGH states, preferably mutually exclusive
one-hot flags. Reset selects HELD. An accepted redirect selects the
appropriate recovery bank; otherwise storage_accept selects NEXT and
no acquisition selects HELD. Every non-reset edge sets the whole token
afresh, with redirect taking priority over acquisition.

The current architectural fetch address A is the token-selected bank,
and drives io_imemAddr, predictor.pc and response.pc consistently.
Compute next_pc from A and the unchanged prediction. Capture next_pc
unconditionally into next_address_q on every edge, without reset, hold,
acquisition or redirect gates. Independently capture A into held_address_q
on every non-reset edge, resetting that bank to zero. These wide bank
updates must not depend on CURRENT combinational redirect, storage_accept,
decode hold, divider_wait or either ready signal. Their speculative data
is harmless because the NEW token selects exactly the architecturally
appropriate candidate sampled on that edge. An imem stall or full queue
immediately after recovery selects HELD, which just captured the correct
recovery address A. Consecutive stalls repeatedly recapture that same A.
Back-to-back corrections select the newest recovery candidate directly.
Thus no copy, acceptance or late hold mux precedes a wide PC register.

Remove redirect from the physical occupancy register as well. Define
logical count_q as zero when the CURRENT token selects either recovery
bank, otherwise stored_count_q. Every queue consumer, head selection,
decode_ready, storage_accept, storage_pop and append_index uses this
logical count. Reset stored_count_q to zero. On every other edge update
stored_count_q from logical count_q plus the existing enqueue/pop delta,
including an explicit stored_count_q<=count_q when both or neither fire.
Do not use stored_count_q as the arithmetic base. On a redirect edge,
speculative old-path occupancy is immediately hidden by the NEW token.
On the next edge, new-path acquisition/admission from logical count zero
materializes the correct stored occupancy before the token leaves the
recovery state. This preserves same-edge flushing without a combinational EX
redirect entering any occupancy reset, enable or data selection.

Complete the same separation at ID/EX: capture raw in.valid independently
of kill into the existing payload-valid register; capture kill into a
separate killed_q sideband using the identical reset and !hold enable.
Expose out.valid=raw_valid_q&&!killed_q. Reset both bits to zero; a genuine
downstream hold retains both. The visible ID/EX bundle must be cycle-for-
cycle identical to today's output, including load-use replay, redirects,
bubbles and divider/dmem holds. No extra squash or execution cycle is
introduced. Keep killed_q out of every wide payload register's controls.

For preselected forwarding eligibility, use next_w_en=in.valid &&
in.ctrl.reg_write && !misalign_jump rather than routing the full
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write cone into forward_unit. This is equivalent for
every decoder-produced control: branches have reg_write=0, and only a
jump's alignment fault can suppress an EX register writer. The complete
branch/jump trap record and EX/MEM control remain ctrl_with_trap as before.
This removes a branch comparison path into younger forwarding decisions
while preserving trap suppression, x0 and youngest-writer priority.

Give this speculative fetch-state machine an independent dequeue
backpressure signal. The IF stall/dequeue input must contain only true
downstream dmem/divider holds and load/multiply replay. Remove !decode_ready
from that signal; it is redundant with IF's own nonempty pop predicate and
imem_ready acquisition predicate. A nonempty queue is ready regardless
of the raw bus, and an empty unready queue cannot acquire or pop anything.
Missing instruction data still produces out.valid=0 and a normal decode
bubble. Keep raw io_imemReady on storage_accept and response validity;
never advance the fetch address for an unaccepted acquisition. Remove
the now-unused hazard-unit fetch-readiness port rather than keeping an
artificial count->decode_ready->hazard->pop/enqueue feedback cone.
This is the dequeue handshake of the same recovery-state machine, not
a change in prediction policy or instruction issue behavior.

Preserve reset priority and exactly the existing visible ID/EX kill behavior. Retain the
queue's ungated payload movement,
fall-through admission, pop/refill accounting and prediction metadata.
Do not postpone squash or recover in MEM: the first target response must
be offered in exactly the same cycle as today. Redirect control drives
only small token/valid state, never physical occupancy or wide address-bank input
selects or write enables. Keep the final bank-selection mux shallow;
explicitly fixed wiring and a one-hot masked-OR implementation are
suitable, provided synthesis retains the separate candidate banks.

Preserve nret=1, the complete top-level IO shape, exactly-once in-order
retirement and stores, decoder legality, traps, retained forwarding,
all memory-ready semantics and every M arithmetic/ALTOPS operation.
Change no predictor policy, divider schedule, proof depth, assumption,
wrapper, benchmark, evaluator or other core. Keep all architectural
assertions; only implementation-specific observations of the old single
PC register may be adapted to the selected architectural address.

Verify equivalence of the selected fetch-address sequence and queue
admissions to the original IF for identical input events, including
reset, redirect coincident with pop/refill, full/empty queues, multiple
consecutive imem stalls, no acquisition immediately after recovery,
and consecutive correction events. Pipeline tests must cover taken
forward branches, backward-loop exits, JAL/JALR, target misalignment,
youngest-writer JALR forwarding, older stalled loads/stores, divider
holds, wrong-path memory suppression and reset during recovery.
Retain the ten-clock branch-to-divide bound unchanged and compare full
RVFI fields and exact-once memory effects with and without bus stalls.
Run unchanged formal, cosim and canonical CoreMark validation, then
compare all vendor placement options using marker-bracketed cycles.

Expect approximately unchanged CoreMark cycles and a 7 percent fitness
improvement from splitting target arithmetic and late recovery control
across independent same-edge captures. At unchanged cycles acceptance
requires median Fmax above 86.34 MHz and fitness above 213.0702.
The post-register address mux and divider prefix/recurrence are the main
timing risks. Preliminary recovery-only banking measured 82.546 MHz;
adding logical occupancy masking measured 83.058 MHz and passed all
53 unchanged single-retire ALTOPS formal checks, eight full-RVFI cosim
runs and canonical stalled CoreMark in exactly 4,052,037 cycles. Those
partial topologies are not the delivered hypothesis: both retain a late
storage_accept/hold mux before the normal PC register. The complete
four-bank prototype measured 83.476 MHz and passed all 53 formal checks
and pipeline/queue tests, but the residual path ended at ID/EX validity.
The delivered hypothesis completes isolation with the separate decode
squash sideband and branch-independent forwarding eligibility described
above. Before independent dequeue control, the decode-token prototype
passed pipeline/queue tests, eight full-RVFI cosim runs and canonical
CoreMark in 4,052,037 cycles, but regressed to 81.692 MHz median. Its
worst path was stored_count_q through IF/hazard back to a payload-bank
write, 17.509 ns through 12 cells. The delivered hypothesis additionally
removes that redundant readiness feedback via the independent dequeue
handshake. Complete-proposal timing has not been measured; earlier probes
do not establish a gain above the required 4.6 percent acceptance gate.

title: Registered prediction recovery with an indirect landing bypass
motivation:
The champion scores 203.70 iter/sec at 82.542 MHz and 4,052,037 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from ID/EX rs1 through EX
to the fetch PC: 17.588 ns and 39 cells. Recovery combines forwarded
operands, JALR target arithmetic, target selection and the fetch-PC mux
on one edge. The r9s2 agreement table and r10s2 local-history table saved
about two percent of cycles but missed qualification after timing costs.
Retiming predictor recovery targets the current bottleneck without a
lookup table on every fetch.

An isolated prototype of the final landing-bypass architecture measured
the original 4,052,037 canonical marked stalled CoreMark cycles. Gowin
placement options 0/1/2 produced 81.919/86.872/86.872 MHz, median 86.872.
This scores 214.391 iter/sec, 5.25 percent above the 203.70 champion and
above the 213.0702 qualification threshold. It passed eight complete
selftest/random RVFI trace comparisons with and without bus stalls,
every canonical CRC/UART/bounds check, lint, all 53 unchanged single-
retire ALTOPS formal checks and all 44 pipeline tests. Pipeline test
observations were adapted for the appended prediction-field offset and
the separated immediate-squash/target signals; every assertion and the
original ready-high JALR and branch-to-divide latency checks were kept.
The implementing agent must rerun the complete gates on its delivered RTL.

An extra-bubble recovery prototype failed the existing symbolic
liveness bound. The final landing bypass preserves the original
recovery latency and passes that check without contract changes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one prediction-recovery architecture that removes the live
forwarded JALR target from fetch-PC feedback without adding a recovery
cycle. Preselect the alternate direct-control PC at ID/EX, and present
a registered indirect target through a one-cycle landing-address bypass.
Retain the existing stateless BTFNT/aligned-JAL prediction policy.

Add a 32-bit direct_recovery_pc above the existing ID/EX payload fields,
preserving their lower offsets. At the normal decode capture edge select
wrapping PC+4 when the exact fetched predicted_taken bit is set, otherwise
wrapping PC+decoded immediate. Compute candidates in parallel before the
registered selection. Retain low bits for arbitrary PCs/immediates, the
existing synchronous reset and downstream hold, and validity-only kills.
This is speculative recovery metadata, not architectural RVFI pc_next.

Keep accepted direct direction-mismatch detection and correction on their
original EX edge. Use direct_recovery_pc as the target, independently of
live branch comparison results. Isolate direct legality/alignment checks
from JALR checks so forwarded indirect operands cannot feed the direct
correction predicate. Preserve existing illegal and misalignment behavior,
link results, resolved architectural next PC and one-bit direct recovery.
Correct predictions and direct misses retain their current cycle counts.

On an accepted valid legal aligned JALR, squash younger ID admission and
flush fetch-queue occupancy immediately, exactly as the current EX
correction does. Capture the full forwarded (rs1+immediate)&~1 target
into an indirect_target_q register and set indirect_landing_q. Qualify
acceptance with !reset, !stall_ex_mem and !divider_wait. An older memory
stall defers capture; invalid, illegal or misaligned JALRs never set it.
Reset clears landing validity and initializes the target payload.
Preserve a capture enable on the target register; an isolated ungated
capture variant lost timing and is excluded from this hypothesis.

Crucially, during the cycle immediately after that capture drive the
instruction bus from fetch_pc = indirect_landing_q ? indirect_target_q :
resident_pc_q. The mux uses only registered control/data. Thus the target
response is available at the same pipeline cycle as the original JALR
recovery, with no extra decode bubble. Use this effective fetch_pc for
response.pc, the direct predictor's lookup PC and sequential PC+4.
The exact instruction and prediction from that bus response must travel
together into the queue or ID/EX.

Clear landing validity on the next edge, independently of imemReady.
At that edge, if storage_accept is true, set resident_pc_q to the landing
response's predicted successor, computed from effective fetch_pc. If no
response was accepted, commit indirect_target_q itself to resident_pc_q,
so a stalled request continues at the same correct address after the
bypass disappears. Do not kill or suppress decode solely because landing
validity is set: a ready correct target must be admitted on that edge.
If decode is independently held, queue the accepted landing response
normally. Never repeat the target, skip its successor or use the stale
resident PC for response metadata or sequential prediction.

Distinguish the immediate squash pulse from a direct resident-PC install
and the registered indirect landing indication. Direct corrections still
have priority over ordinary acquisitions and install their registered
alternate PC on the resolving edge. A JALR squash clears occupancy and
invalidates simultaneous wrong-path admission; it must not send its live
target sum into the resident-PC data mux. The resident PC may make one
harmless speculative acquisition on this squash edge: pending landing
overrides its bus address on the next cycle and replaces its state when
the landing response is handled. All payload writes on squash remain
unreachable after occupancy clears. Keep occupancy recovery separate
from packed payload-bank writes and their enables.

Preserve nret=1 and every top-level port, default-illegal decoding,
alignment traps, resolved architectural RVFI PCs, contiguous retirement,
exact-once links/stores, bounded memory, M arithmetic/ALTOPS, eight-edge
division, retained WB forwarding and existing load/multiply replays.
Do not add a direction table, return stack, BTB, pipeline stage or bubble,
or weaken any formal depth, assumption, assertion or timing deadline.

Retain all architectural assertions, the ten-clock ready-high branch-to-
divide bound and existing ready-high JALR-to-target retirement gap.
Update prediction-bit observations and packed builders to account for
the appended field, preserving the assertions' meaning. Independently
verify alternate-PC selection, signed immediates, 32-bit wrap and low-bit
faults. Cover EX/MEM- and MEM/WB-forwarded JALR bases, x0/link aliases,
bit-0 clearing, bit-1 traps, reserved funct3, consecutive transfers,
reset around capture/landing, full/empty queues and every bus/M/load hold.
Specifically verify ready landing acquisition advances to its own
predicted successor, unready landing commits its target, metadata uses
effective fetch_pc, no extra JALR bubble and no wrong-path store or link.

Run unchanged lint, unit, all 53 single-retire ALTOPS formal checks,
complete selftest/random RVFI comparisons with and without stalls,
canonical marked stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds validation and all
three Gowin placements. The isolated final prototype retains the original
4,052,037 marked cycles, uses 5,901 logic cells and 2,101 registers on
placement option 0, and retains four BSRAMs, six DSPs and zero LUT-RAMs.
Qualification requires fitness above 213.0702 iter/sec, approximately
86.339 MHz at unchanged cycles. The measured 86.872 MHz median of the
final prototype clears this target, with a limited margin that requires
preserving the measured topology during implementation.
The new fetch-address mux, ID alternate-PC arithmetic and remaining
divider/ALU/queue routing are the main timing risks.

title: Select fetch-source operands after parallel register-file reads
motivation:
The champion reaches 216.47 iter/sec at 87.715 MHz and 4,052,037 marked

title: Two-bank operand delivery with queued source predecode
motivation: The champion scores 216.47 iter/sec at 87.715 MHz with 4,052,037 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from fetch-queue occupancy through the RF into ID/EX rs2: 16.717 ns and ten cells. Queue selection currently precedes binary source decode and the complete read tree. The successful r3s1 structural attempt established explicit RF flip-flops and validity-only squash; preserve both. Isolated four-candidate RF reads preserved CoreMark cycles but used 7,256 logic cells and reached only 83.089 MHz median. Moving the high-select gate after four eight-word reductions used 5,806 cells and reached 85.950 MHz. The proposed topology instead combines a two-bank read organization with queued low-address predecode to remove occupancy-dependent decoding without four full read networks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the fetch-to-RF operand boundary as two sixteen-word RF read banks fed by source predecode carried with queued instructions. This is one structural operand-delivery architecture. It keeps one physical 31-word flip-flop RF, two combinational read ports, one write port, the existing ID/EX capture edge and every instruction's latency. The two parts are complementary: predecode removes the binary-address comparator after queue selection; late bank selection keeps that predecode to sixteen bits per source rather than thirty-two and shares a single pair of physical read networks.

In IF compute sixteen one-hot low-offset selects for each raw source field: rs1 uses imem_data[18:15] and rs2 uses imem_data[23:20]. Predecode the raw response independently of count, stall, redirect, reset and validity. Carry the resulting 32-bit sidecar through four fixed fetch-queue banks, shifting and appending under exactly the same payload movement/enqueue conditions as instruction, PC and prediction. Append must win over shifting at its destination, including sole-entry replacement and full pop/refill. Like the existing speculative payload, sidecar storage has no reset/recovery gates: occupancy alone determines reachability. Do not alter the existing packed if_id_t layout or its validity semantics.

Present head-sidecar rs1/rs2 low selects when count_q is nonzero and raw-response low selects otherwise, using precisely the instruction's existing head/fallthrough selector. Carry only register-address predecode, never sampled operand values: actual RF state and WB write-first bypass must be observed on decode admission after arbitrary holds. Preserve the original selected five-bit source tags for forwarding, hazards, x0, bank selection and RVFI. The low-select sidecar is functional metadata associated with those exact tags, including unused instruction source-field aliases.

In RF, organize fixed-index words 0..15 and 16..31 into two read banks. Mask each word only with the incoming low-select bit indexed by register_number modulo sixteen. Read both banks in parallel with balanced OR reductions, then select bank zero or one using the original selected source address bit four. Apply the existing x0 priority and same-cycle WB bypass independently on both ports, without changing their architectural semantics. Keep reset-over-write priority and existing write decoders. There is no bank conflict: any pair of sources, equal or different, within or across banks is legal in one cycle.

Use explicit fixed-index pair leaves and balanced reductions. A pair of (word_bit & low_select) terms fits a LUT4; do not reintroduce the high bank bit or full five-bit equality into these leaves. The low selection must arrive directly from IF sidecar/fallthrough predecode, never be re-decoded from the muxed binary source address. Keep high-bank selection after the local read tree. Retain explicit per-word flip-flops, not arrays eligible for RAM inference or synchronous read-output absorption. Add no RF output register or pipeline stage.

Wire the two low-select vectors from IF directly into RF in core. ID still receives the original selected instruction/PC/prediction and current RF operands, and captures exactly as before. Preserve queue acquisition and flush rules, accepted ready/unready JALR landing behavior, direct recovery, load/multiply replay, retained WB bypass during stalls, eight-edge division, real M arithmetic and ALTOPS, decoder default-illegal rules, all traps, contiguous retirement and exact-once memory effects. Keep nret=1, core's complete top-level IO, memory bounds, every original assertion and ready-high JALR/branch-to-divide retirement deadline. Change no evaluator, benchmark, formal assumption/depth, wrapper or core.yaml contract.

Validate each selected low vector against one shifted by the corresponding admitted instruction's source low bits in the independent deque model, including every occupancy, empty bypass, full hold/pop/refill, redirects, changing unready bus data, reset and indirect landings. Keep all RF assertions, adapting only fixture wiring to derive low selects independently from binary test addresses. Exercise all 1,024 address pairs, same/cross-bank sources, x0, all destinations and WB bypass on either/both ports against the independent RF model. Run original pipeline tests, unchanged single-retire formal and full selftest/random RVFI comparisons in ready-high and stalled modes. Require canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds validation and the same 4,052,037 marker-bracketed cycles.

Measure all three vendor Gowin placements. Verify that occupancy no longer traverses binary low-source equality before the RF read reduction, that bank selection remains late, and that the RF still uses zero BSRAMs with unchanged writable-word storage. The nominal overhead is 128 sidecar FFs, partly pruned by synthesis, with less read logic than duplicating full RF networks. Qualification requires fitness above 226.42762 iter/sec or approximately 91.74931 MHz at unchanged cycles. Shared low-select fanout, sidecar placement, selected-address WB bypass and competing EX/divider paths are the main risks. This expected gain requires the complete topology and full evaluator gates; the earlier read-network probes do not establish a qualifying improvement.

title: Balanced shared branch comparison with XOR sign correction
motivation:
The champion scores 216.47 iter/sec at 87.715 MHz with 4,052,037
marked CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path is occupancy-to-RF,
but the r12s0/r12s2 duplicate-read attempts and r12s1 source sidecars
lost timing while exposing long forwarded-operand-to-fetch-recovery
paths. Local RF probes in this worktree also reduced LUTs without
improving timing. The execute stage separately expresses equality,
signed less-than/greater-or-equal and unsigned comparisons before a
branch-op selection mux. A shared balanced comparison can shorten
direct direction recovery without extra state, bubbles or queue wiring.

hypothesis.motivation:

marked CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path is occupancy-to-RF,
but the r12s0/r12s2 duplicate-read attempts and r12s1 source sidecars

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only EX branch-condition computation. Build one shared
combinational lexicographic comparator that produces equality and
unsigned less-than from the forwarded rs1 and rs2 values. Divide each
operand into sixteen adjacent two-bit slices. At every leaf compute
equal_i = (a_i == b_i) and less_i = (a_i < b_i) independently. Combine
adjacent low/high slices through four balanced levels with
equal = equal_high && equal_low and
less = less_high || (equal_high && less_low).
Higher-numbered slices are always more significant. Use fixed-index
generated wires and small Boolean nodes; no ripple across all sixteen
slices, wide subtractor, dynamic lookup, RAM or additional registers.
These two-bit leaf predicates each depend on four data inputs and
suit LUT4 mapping. The comparison tree reads exactly the existing
forwarded functional operands, including retained WB data during holds.

Derive signed_less = unsigned_less ^ rs1[31] ^ rs2[31], avoiding a
separate signed comparator or sign-difference-controlled data mux.
Keep an explicit paired case for selecting the shared predicate:
BR_BEQ/BR_BNE select equality, BR_BLT/BR_BGE select signed_less,
and BR_BLTU/BR_BGEU select unsigned_less; default selects false.
For legal branch funct3 values XOR the selected predicate with
branch_op[0] to obtain BNE/BGE/BGEU inversion; force branch_cond false
for reserved 010/011. Keep the existing is_branch gate and default-
illegal decoder validation. Preserve the explicit three-family case
topology: an isolated fully fused funct3/sign/polarity formulation
measured only 84.965 MHz median and is excluded from this proposal.
Signed less-than equals unsigned less-than XOR the sign difference
for every RV32 operand pair, including sign boundaries and equality.

Keep direct_taken, legal/alignment qualification, control acceptance,
redirect timing and recovery targets otherwise identical. Keep all
ALU operations, effective-address arithmetic, JAL/JALR targets and link
values, actual and ALTOPS M arithmetic, eight-edge division, multiply
replay, RF reads, fetch queue and bus-stall handling unchanged. Add no
instruction latency or architectural state. Preserve nret=1, every
top-level port, traps, exact-once memory effects, contiguous in-order
retirement, raw RVFI source reporting and all existing test deadlines.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 31 writable 32-bit FF words and their full masked-OR read
networks with replicated asynchronous distributed RAM. Make two identical
physical RF copies, one for each read port, written identically by the
existing single WB port. Split each copy into two 16-word by 32-bit banks;
read both banks using the source address low four bits and select the
final bank using address bit four. Every pair of source registers remains
available in the same cycle, including two addresses in the same bank.

Use generic synthesizable SV arrays with synchronous writes and genuinely
combinational reads, plus Gowin's distributed-RAM inference attribute.
Do not reset or initialize the RAM arrays and do not add RAM read/output
registers. Use a 32-bit per-word written-valid FF vector with x0 permanently
invalid. Synchronous reset clears the valid vector; an actual nonzero WB
write sets its destination bit. A read of an unwritten register returns
zero regardless of arbitrary physical RAM contents. RAM data writes may
occur during reset harmlessly, since reset has priority in valid tracking
and makes those contents unobservable until a subsequent actual write.
Both RAM copies always receive identical address/data/enables. Do not use
an epoch bit whose wrap could expose stale data after repeated resets.

Preserve the exact read priority independently on each port: x0 returns
zero first, a same-cycle enabled matching WB write returns w_data second,
otherwise return RAM data if the selected register is valid and zero if
invalid. The WB bypass must work even for a destination's first post-reset
write, before its valid bit rises. Ignore writes to x0 in both RAM copies
and valid tracking. Keep reset synchronous and preserve all existing RF
port semantics, raw unused-source aliases, and reset-over-write behavior.
Mask unknown/uninitialized RAM contents with validity so no X reaches
observable operands before their first write.

Keep source addresses from the existing selected instruction and preserve
all queue capacity, bank movement, fallthrough, branch prediction/recovery,
ready/unready JALR landing, hazard/replay, forwarding and instruction
latencies. Keep ID/EX as the real operand capture boundary outside RAM.

with a synchronous output or absorption of ID/EX registers. Confirm this
in Gowin synthesis/resource reports rather than assuming an attribute
worked. Reuse the original selected address tags for hazards and RVFI.
No source sidecar, added general pipeline stage or duplicate FF RF is
part of the proposal.

title: One-bit local correlation with a cached agreement lookup
motivation:
The champion reaches 216.47 iterations/second at 87.715 MHz and
4,052,037 marked CoreMark cycles with stateless BTFNT/JAL prediction.
Earlier agreement and local-history predictors saved about two percent
of cycles, but the 64-bank local-history implementation added 704
state bits and exposed fetch-PC/predictor feedback as a timing limit.
Recent parallel operand reads also lost timing. Capture short repeating
branch patterns with a much smaller predictor and a single cached-bit
lookup, keeping the champion's entire queue and recovery topology.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one eight-bank, one-bit resolved-local-history agreement predictor.
Index fetch and training by PC[4:2] XOR PC[7:5]. Each fixed bank contains
one resolved history bit H, two two-bit saturating agreement counters
C[0..1], and one cached agreement bit A: six bits per bank, 48 bits total.
Reset H to zero, both counters to strong agreement (3), and A to one.
For legal aligned conditional branches predict instr[31] XOR !A[index].
This learns both branch bias and alternating/two-context behavior while
reducing history, counter and lookup state relative to the prior
two-history-bit, 64-bank attempt. Do not add a second predictor mechanism.

Fetch reads only the eight cached disagreement bits through fixed index
equality terms and a balanced OR reduction. No history-to-pattern serial
lookup is allowed on the fetch path. Keep the current 30-bit B/J target
addition, wrapping semantics, validated branch funct3 set, PC alignment,
immediate bit-1 guard, aligned JAL always taken, and JALR sequential.
Targets always come from the actual fetched instruction, so aliases
affect prediction accuracy without compromising correctness.

Train once from accepted registered EX/MEM branch metadata:
ex_mem_w.valid && !reset && !hold_mem_wb && ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_branch &&
!ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_illegal && ex_mem_w.pc[1:0]==0 && !ex_mem_w.instr[8].
Use this branch's own PC, instr[31] and branch_taken. Do not feed live
forwarded EX operands, redirect, bus acquisition or speculative history
into training. Define G=(branch_taken==instr[31]); saturate only C[H]
toward G. Hnext=branch_taken. On the same edge store A=Cnext[Hnext][1],
including the updated counter when Hnext==H. Adjacent accepted updates
at one bank must observe the preceding edge's new state.

Implement independent fixed flip-flop banks and constant-index counter
wiring. For old high/low bits h,l use exact saturating Boolean equations
hnext=(h&l)|(G&(h|l)), lnext=(h&~l)|(G&(h|~l)). Compute both pattern
candidates locally, update only the old-history counter, and select the
next cached MSB locally using Hnext. Avoid RAM inference, global training
muxes, tags, target storage and wide reset or forwarding additions.

Preserve the exact prediction saved with each acquired queue response
through ID/EX; compare that saved bit with actual direction in EX, never
reread predictor state during resolution. Keep binary queue occupancy,
all four packed payload banks, empty fallthrough, payload write enables,
occupancy-only squash and existing hazard/forwarding rules unchanged.
Keep preselected direct recovery, immediate JALR squash, registered
indirect landing, ready landing acquisition and unready target commit.
Nonspeculative history requires no rollback or new queue metadata.

Retain nret=1 and every top-level port, decoder default-illegal rules,
alignment traps, architectural RVFI next PCs, contiguous exact-once
retirement and memory/link effects, retained WB forwarding, load/MUL
replays, MUL/DIV arithmetic and ALTOPS. Preserve all formal assumptions,
depths, assertions and existing architectural latency bounds.

Retain exhaustive direct-target, wrap, reserved-encoding and alignment
tests. Check cold BTFNT behavior after reset and use an independent
integer state model for learned prediction. Exhaust both histories,
every counter combination, both biases and outcomes, next-context
update bypass, aliases, back-to-back same-bank updates, reset and
suppressed training on invalid/illegal/held payloads. Cover acquisition
followed by later predictor changes, alternating branches, loop exits,
forward branches, bus/load/M holds and wrong-path stores. Keep full
architectural PC/order/operand checks and all latency limits; adapt
observations that specifically assumed an untrained static prediction
to the independent predictor model, preserving their assertion meaning.

Run unchanged lint/unit/formal/cosim gates, canonical marker-bracketed
stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds validation and all three Gowin placements.
Qualification requires more than 226.42762 iterations/second. Cycle
savings alone are expected below the 4.6 percent threshold; the compact
cached lookup must also preserve or improve Fmax. Hash aliasing and
additional fetch-PC feedback are the main risks. Expected impact is
an estimate until final vendor timing and measured cycles are available.

title: Decode fetch-queue append destinations before the hazard decision
motivation:
The champion scores 216.47 iterations/sec at 87.715 MHz with
4,052,037 marked CoreMark cycles. r12s1 exposed a queue occupancy through
source hazard, hold and append path into a payload sidecar; other RF
and branch changes also exposed queue-control timing. Isolated smaller
operand/recovery probes in this turn passed functional checks but missed
qualification, with fetch-queue payload writes again limiting timing.
The existing append destination subtracts the late pop decision from
three-bit count and then decodes it, placing arithmetic and destination
selection after decode hazard logic. Factor that exact Boolean function
into constant per-bank occupancy predicates before the late stall bit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local combinational control optimization in if_stage; keep
the four-entry queue, binary occupancy register, payload banks, empty
fallthrough, prediction and every acquisition/recovery rule unchanged.
Replace append_index = count_q - (storage_pop ? 1 : 0) and its case
statement with four fixed bank append enables. For bank k=0..3 use
append_enable[k] = imem_ready &&
                  (((count_q == k) && stall) ||
                   ((count_q == k+1) && !stall)).
Use explicitly sized three-bit constants and fixed-index generated wires.
These equalities are computed directly from registered occupancy, in
parallel with the fetch/head selection and hazard path. The late stall
bit chooses already-decoded candidate destinations, avoiding a three-bit
subtract and a subsequent variable append-index decoder.

For count=0, only a held decode enqueues the ready raw response in bank
0; an unheld response falls through and writes no bank. For count=1..3,
a hold appends at bank count while a pop/refill appends at count-1. For
count=4, a hold writes no bank and a ready pop/refill writes bank3. With
imem_ready=0 no bank appends, but an occupied unheld queue still shifts
and drains. Retain the current shift assignments on storage_pop and
let each bank's append assignment override its shift, exactly as today.
Do not put reset, redirect or validity gates on payload-bank writes;
occupancy-only flush makes speculative writes unreachable.

Keep storage_pop, storage_accept, storage_bypass and storage_enqueue
semantics for PC acquisition and occupancy updates. In particular PC
must advance only on the existing storage_accept, independent of decode
consumption, and count must update only on the same enqueue/pop pair.
Retain storage_enqueue if needed for occupancy even though payload
writes now use direct bank predicates. Remove the unused append_index
signal and the arithmetic/case datapath entirely. Do not add sidecar
state, extra RF reads, a new FIFO representation or any instruction
stage. This is Boolean factoring of existing queue destination control,
not a new memory architecture or predictor.

Keep the raw response PC/prediction fields, full pop/refill behavior,
append-over-shift priority, no-wait empty bypass, direct recovery PC
preselection, immediate indirect squash and registered JALR landing.
Ready landing responses predict their own successors; an unaccepted
landing commits its target before the bypass disappears. Preserve every
load-use and multiply replay, true dmem/divider hold, retained WB bypass,
actual/ALTOPS arithmetic, eight-edge division, default-illegal decoding,
trap/alignment gate, nret=1 port and RVFI contract, contiguous retirement,
exact-once memory effect and every existing test/latency assertion.

Check the new per-bank enables against the original queue transaction
semantics for all legal occupancies 0..4, both stall values and both
imem_ready values, and compare complete payload order with the existing
independent deque model. Cover append-only, pop-only, simultaneous
pop/refill at every occupied depth, full hold, empty bypass, prolonged
backpressure, live imem changes while unready, reset/redirect with
speculative writes and ready/unready indirect landing. Preserve content,
PC, prediction and acquisition assertions, not just enable equivalence.

formal and full-RVFI cosim with and without bus stalls. Require canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks and exactly 4,052,037 marked
cycles, then all three Gowin placements. Qualification at unchanged
cycles requires over 226.42762 iterations/sec, approximately 91.749 MHz
median Fmax. Predicate fanout, payload shift mux routing and competing
RF/divider/branch paths can limit the gain; vendor timing must establish
whether this factoring removes enough delay to clear the margin.

passed strict Verilator lint, the existing independent fetch-queue model,
and the complete pipeline suite. It also passed all eight full-RVFI
selftest/random comparisons with and without bus stalls. Canonical
stalled CoreMark passed all CRC/UART/bounds/completion gates and retained
markers 14,406 and 4,066,443, exactly 4,052,037 measured cycles. These
results support functional equivalence of the control factoring;
implementation must rerun the complete evaluator gates and vendor
fitness measurement on the delivered RTL. The Fmax gain remains a
prediction until the placement measurements complete.

title: Registered recovery tokens with independent fetch acquisition credit
motivation:
The champion reaches 216.47 iter/sec at 87.715 MHz. Its queue occupancy
feeds decode operand selection, while recent RF and predictor attempts
repeatedly exposed forwarded operands feeding fetch recovery and queue
control. More RF ports and source sidecars lost timing; distributed RF
alone gained only 2.49 percent. Isolate the fetch producer from live EX
recovery and consumer backpressure with one registered recovery boundary.

hypothesis.motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the four-entry fallthrough fetch queue and binary occupancy
organization, but place all control-flow recovery behind one registered
landing token. Generalize the existing registered JALR landing mechanism
to accepted direct direction corrections as well. On the resolving edge,
EX still kills the younger ID/EX instruction immediately, but records
only a one-bit recovery-valid token. Capture the corresponding recovery
PC every normal clock, selecting the existing ID/EX.direct_recovery_pc
for direct corrections or the forwarded, bit-zero-cleared JALR sum for
indirect transfers. Do not gate this 32-bit capture with late redirect,
branch comparison, legality or alignment decisions. The registered
valid token alone determines whether that captured target is observable.
Its reset remains synchronous. Preserve all existing acceptance,
legality, misalignment, prediction-hit and trap qualifications on the
token; correctly predicted direct controls generate no token.

During the following landing cycle, override io_imemAddr with the
registered target for either kind of recovery. Remove the immediate
direct_redirect mux and enable from the resident-PC register. A ready
landing advances resident_pc to its own predicted or sequential
successor; an unaccepted landing commits the landing target before the
bypass disappears. This fetches the correct target on exactly the same
cycle as the existing direct-PC update and registered JALR landing.
Keep the original static predictor and recovery-PC calculation.

Retiming queue invalidation is essential to the same boundary. Do not
reset or flush the stored occupancy on the live EX redirect. Instead,
the registered landing token makes the old queue logically empty:
head_present = NOT landing AND (stored_count != 0), and
full = NOT landing AND (stored_count == 4).
Drive decode_ready from head_present OR imem_ready and select the
registered head versus the raw response with head_present. Use these
direct predicates, rather than adding an effective-count mux before a
comparator or before operand reads. On the landing edge, replace stored
occupancy with one if a ready response must be queued because decode
holds, otherwise zero. A landing may thus fall through directly or
retain its response, while every stale entry remains unreachable.
Reset clears occupancy and the token. Payload writes remain independent
of live redirect/reset and retain append-over-shift priority. Use a
derived effective count solely for verification if existing tests need
the count_q observation. No epoch wrapping or speculative retirement.

Allocate fetch credit from registered occupancy alone:
accept = imem_ready AND NOT full. In particular, a queue that starts the
cycle full declines acquisition even when decode pops that cycle; the
producer uses that freed credit starting on the next cycle. This removes
live load/MUL dependency checks, divider wait and decode backpressure
from the resident-PC acquisition enable. Consumer pop remains
head_present AND NOT stall. Empty ready/no-stall responses still fall
through without enqueueing. A full pop shifts/decrements without refill;
every other producer/consumer case retains ordinary bounded FIFO
behavior. This policy intentionally spends occasional fetch credit to
break the consumer-to-producer control path, without dropping an
instruction or a response the core claimed to accept. Do not add a
pipeline stage, change queue capacity, change the RF, or alter M engines.

This is one structural retiming of the front-end recovery/acquisition
boundary. The binary queue avoids the high-fanout unary-valid variant
explored locally. Conservative credit with unified landing passed
ready-high/stalled selftest cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC,
UART and bounds validation in a preliminary unary-queue probe. It used
4,053,618 marked cycles, just 1,581 or 0.039 percent above the champion.
That probe did not improve timing and does not establish acceptance.
The delivered hypothesis retains binary queue storage/control and direct
head/full predicates; all three Gowin placements and complete correctness
gates must validate this final form. At this cycle count qualification
needs median Fmax above approximately 91.79 MHz and fitness above
226.43 iter/sec. RF, base-ALU and divider paths remain competing limits.

Preserve nret=1 and every core IO, default-illegal decode, all alignment
and SYSTEM traps, contiguous exact-once retirement, raw RVFI source
values, exact-once memory effects, memory bounds, eight-edge division,
MEM multiplication, real M arithmetic and ALTOPS. Change no evaluator,
benchmark, wrapper, formal depth/assumption, core.yaml contract or
architectural assertion. Preserve the existing ten-clock ready-high
branch-to-divide retirement bound and all other retirement deadlines.

Use an independent bounded-deque oracle with the explicit start-of-cycle
credit policy, and retain every payload-order, PC, no-loss and no-duplicate
assertion. Cover all occupancies and ready/hold combinations, full pop
without refill, the next-cycle credit, empty fallthrough, direct and
indirect landings, ready prediction on landing, unready landing
continuity, stale queued instructions, back-to-back recovery, reset and
wrong-path stores. Internal landing/occupancy assertions must reflect
the new registered boundary while retaining architectural checks.

RVFI cosimulation, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds validation and all
three Gowin timing builds. Verify marker-bracketed cycles and resource
counts; the expected improvement remains an estimate until measured.

Remove this live resolving event from IF queue occupancy, resident-PC
enables and ID validity. The resolving edge may therefore admit one
younger wrong-path instruction into ID/EX. During the immediately
following cycle the registered recovery flag squashes that younger EX
slot before it can enter EX/MEM, launch DIV/REM, advertise a forwarding
producer or generate another correction. Treat it as invalid for every

Do not freeze it: advance an EX/MEM bubble while the resolving control

title: One MEM multiplier with registered signedness expansion
motivation:
The champion reaches 216.47 iterations/sec at 87.715 MHz and 4,052,037
marked CoreMark cycles. Prior micro_opt attempts show that custom carry
structures and extra operand muxing can worsen Gowin timing, while
registered arithmetic operands and early result selection have worked.
The current physical MEM multiplier evaluates three 64-bit products
for signed/signed, unsigned/unsigned and signed/unsigned operations,
then selects their halves. This uses six reported DSP resources.
A single multiplier with explicitly expanded signedness can implement
all four RV32M multiply instructions and reduce product-selection
wiring and DSP pressure without changing scheduling or replay latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the three physical MEM product expressions with one signed
33-by-33-bit multiplier. Prepare operand-extension bits and the selected
result half before the existing EX/MEM edge. This is one local
multiplier representation and selection optimization; retain pipeline
stages, memory protocols, branch prediction, forwarding, divider and
multiply scheduling exactly as in the champion.

Add three sideband fields at the most-significant end of ex_mem_t so
existing lower packed-field offsets remain unchanged. On the same
normal edge that captures multiply_a=forwarded rs1 and multiply_b=
forwarded rs2, capture a_sign=((alu_op==MULH || alu_op==MULHSU) &&
rs1[31]), b_sign=(alu_op==MULH && rs2[31]), and select_low=(alu_op==MUL).
Reset these fields to zero, and hold them with the entire EX/MEM
payload during a genuine dmem stall. A divider-wait bubble retains
today's payload behavior and clears valid as before. No new stage,
request handshake, arithmetic latency, dependency rule or consumer
bubble is introduced.

In multiplier form signed 33-bit A=$signed({a_sign,a}) and
B=$signed({b_sign,b}), then explicitly declare signed product[65:0]
and compute product=A*B exactly once. For a legal multiply operation
select product[31:0] when select_low is true and product[63:32]
otherwise. Keep result=0 for all nonmultiply op encodings. Bit 65:64
is redundant for the architectural extraction but must not influence
width or signedness inference. Use the full 66-bit expression and
exact bit slices, not a truncated 32-bit product or a high-half
approximation. Low MUL uses zero extension of both raw 32-bit words;
its low half equals the signed low half modulo 2^32. MULHU zero-extends
both operands, MULH sign-extends both, and MULHSU sign-extends only A.

The extra sign and half-select bits are registered controls, so no
MEM opcode comparator precedes a multiplier operand-extension bit or
the high/low selector. mem_stage passes them directly to multiplier.
Preserve its existing is_multiply eligibility, load-versus-product
MEM/WB selection, retained WB data, trap suppression and retirement
validity. These flags are meaningful only with their matching payload;
they never create a producer or memory effect on their own.

Leave the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU formulas and
their accepted raw operands unchanged. The original op still selects
the ALTOPS formula, independently of extension controls. Leave the
standalone ALU's registered multiply implementation and handshake
unchanged; its real and ALTOPS outputs must remain bit-identical to
the physical MEM multiplier for every valid instruction. Do not change
division, base ALU arithmetic, decoder legality, source-use rules,
branch/memory alignment traps, fetch queue, register-file storage,
nret=1 core IO, RVFI, contiguous order or exact-once memory effects.

An isolated single-product prototype with live MEM sign decoding
passed strict lint, real and ALTOPS multiplier tests and the complete
pipeline suite. Gowin inferred two DSP resources instead of six, but
that simpler variant's median timing was below the champion. The
proposed refinement registers expansion and result-half controls at
the existing EX/MEM edge to avoid that variant's live control cones.
The expected fitness gain is an estimate, not an acceptance claim;
competing fetch/RF/divider paths and DSP placement may still limit it.
At unchanged cycles qualification needs median Fmax above about
91.75 MHz and fitness above 226.43 iterations/sec.

Preserve all existing multiplier vectors and independent arbitrary-
precision references. Verify both sign-extension bits, selected half
and raw forwarded operands remain associated through consecutive MUL
variants, invalid bubbles, resets and prolonged dmem holds. Include
all signedness combinations of zero, one, minus one, INT_MIN,
INT_MAX and UINT_MAX, and random high-half products, especially
MULHSU with negative A and B having bit 31 set. Retain all existing
latency, RVFI raw-source, replay and memory-effect assertions. Extend
any direct-module test wiring and packed EX/MEM observation to account
for the new sidebands without dropping assertions on original fields.

Run unchanged lint, real/ALTOPS multiplier and ALU tests, pipeline
tests, single-retire formal, ready-high and stalled full-RVFI cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker gates and all three Gowin
placements. Require unchanged 4,052,037 marked cycles, one-cycle MEM
product computation and existing load/MUL replay bounds. ALTOPS
formal proves routing rather than real multiplication; validate the
actual product with unit vectors and cosim, and use formal-deep or a
local real-product equivalence proof when tractable. Change no formal
assumption, depth, wrapper, benchmark, evaluator or invariant.

title: Decouple fetch acquisition with a registered head and circular tail
motivation:
The champion scores 216.47 at 87.715 MHz and 4,052,037 marked CoreMark
cycles. Prior source sidecars and extra RF read networks worsened the
occupancy-to-hazard-to-payload feedback path. Registered recovery alone
also missed qualification. The current four-entry shift queue moves
three wide payload banks on each dequeue and computes append destinations
from occupancy minus the live pop decision. A FIFO with a registered
head and independently addressed tail can reduce this wide control
fanout while preserving the fast registered head seen by decode.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 216.47 at 87.715 MHz and 4,052,037 marked CoreMark
cycles. Prior source sidecars and extra RF read networks worsened the
occupancy-to-hazard-to-payload feedback path. Registered recovery alone
also missed qualification. The current four-entry shift queue moves
three wide payload banks on each dequeue and computes append destinations
from occupancy minus the live pop decision. A FIFO with a registered
head and independently addressed tail can reduce this wide control
fanout while preserving the fast registered head seen by decode.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the shifting fetch queue with one registered decode-head entry
and a four-entry circular tail, for five total resident instructions.
This is one structural producer/consumer queue architecture. Preserve
empty-response fallthrough, static prediction, current direct recovery
and registered JALR landing, and every execution-stage latency. The
extra tail entry supplies acquisition slack while removing full-pop
refill feedback from the producer's credit decision.

Retain a single small binary total-occupancy register with range zero
through five. Admission credit is computed solely from registered
occupancy: accept = imem_ready && count < 5. A queue beginning a cycle
full declines acquisition even if decode pops; the freed credit becomes
available next cycle. Advance the fetch PC only for actual acquisition,
with the original direct-recovery priority and unready JALR-target
commitment. Never consume unavailable bus data or lose a declined
response by advancing its address.

The registered head remains the only occupied-queue payload presented
to decode. An empty queue presents the raw response exactly as today.
With count zero and decode able to consume, a ready response bypasses
storage. With count zero and decode held, acquisition fills the head.
With count one, simultaneous pop and acquisition replace the head
directly; a held head plus acquisition appends to the tail. With count
greater than one, a pop refills the head from the oldest tail entry,
and a simultaneous acquisition appends independently to the tail.
With no acquisition, a sole-entry pop simply makes occupancy zero.

Store tail entries in four fixed 66-bit FF banks, each containing the
exact prediction bit, PC, instruction, and payload-valid layout. Use
independent four-bit one-hot read and write pointers, rotating by fixed
wiring only on tail dequeue or tail enqueue. Decode tail write enables
directly from the registered write-pointer bits. Select the next head
with four fixed masked terms and a balanced OR tree controlled by the
registered read pointer. This mux precedes head storage, not decode or
RF reads. Never shift tail payloads, derive their append address from
count minus pop, or add a variable-index tail mux after head storage.

Tail enqueue occurs only when an acquisition needs storage and does
not fill or replace the head. Tail dequeue occurs only when decode
pops with more than one resident entry. Update total occupancy from
the existing enqueue-versus-pop accounting, with empty bypass excluded.
On reset or accepted redirect clear occupancy and reset both pointers
to their first bank. Keep these small reachability controls separate
from all payload-bank writes. As in the champion, speculative writes on
reset/redirect may occur but remain unreachable after occupancy clears.
Preserve append-over-refill priority when the sole head is replaced.

Preserve the existing IF decode-ready semantics and external imem
handshake. Keep the current hazard-unit stall input; do not combine
this change with new forwarding, RF, prediction, recovery-token, ALU,
multiplier, or divider architectures. True dmem/divider holds retain
ID/EX while the FIFO may acquire to its bounded capacity. Load/MUL
replay keeps the head instruction until admission. Direct and indirect
recovery discard every stale resident entry while accepting ready
landing responses and committing unready landing addresses as today.

Preserve nret=1 and every external core port, default-illegal decoding,
all SYSTEM and alignment traps, contiguous exact-once retirement,
exact-once memory effects, memory bounds, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART
validation, and marker-only timing. Keep real M arithmetic and ALTOPS,
eight-edge division, MEM multiplication, retained WB forwarding, and
every existing architectural assertion and retirement-latency deadline.
No evaluator, wrapper, benchmark, formal depth or assumption changes
are permitted.

Test with an independent deque oracle using five-entry capacity and
explicit start-of-cycle producer credit. Retain no-loss, no-duplicate,
payload association, accepted-PC, and recovery assertions. Exhaust
every occupancy, ready/hold combination, empty bypass, sole replacement,
full-pop credit delay, simultaneous tail pop/push, pointer wrap, repeated
queue fill/drain, direct redirect, ready/unready JALR landing, reset,
and speculative payload writes on squash. Prove count never exceeds
five and pointers remain one-hot in reachable states. Internal tests
of the old shifting layout or full-pop refill must be replaced with
equally strong queue-order and acceptance checks for the new topology;
no architectural or latency assertion may be relaxed.

Run lint, queue/pipeline tests, all unchanged single-retire formal checks,
full ready-high and stalled RVFI selftest/random cosim, canonical
marker-bracketed stalled CoreMark, and all three Gowin placements.
Measure the actual cycle count: credit policy and capacity change can
alter acquisition timing, so unchanged cycles are not assumed.
Qualification requires fitness above 226.42762 iter/sec; at approximately
4.05 million marked cycles this needs about 91.8 MHz median Fmax.

The timing claim is reduced dequeue/append fanout and shallower producer
bank enables, with one extra payload bank costing roughly 66 FFs and
only a small pointer increase. Principal risks are the head-refill mux,
added storage placement, pointer/occupancy routing, and competing
RF/base-ALU/divider paths. Isolated ordinary-operand and comparator-bank
probes failed to improve timing and are excluded. The final five-entry,
four-tail-bank design has not been vendor-timed; the expected gain is
an estimate requiring the complete implementation and evaluation gates.

title: Issue predicted equality branches before load data returns
motivation:
The champion's BTFNT/JAL predictor already selects a speculative fetch
path, but a conditional branch immediately consuming a LOAD
still inserts an operand-wait bubble before it can enter EX. Earlier
direction/history tables saved only one to two percent of cycles and
lost FPGA timing. Exploit the prediction already present instead of
adding another fetch lookup: issue the waiting branch using its carried
direction and validate its operands one stage later.

An independent reference-ISS run of canonical 2K, -O3 CoreMark counted
2,922,015 instructions between the markers, 529,588 conditional branches,
and 135,320 branches immediately dependent on a LOAD. Every one of
these is BEQ or BNE: 77,300 BEQs and 58,020 BNEs. Of those, 105,590
agree with BTFNT and 29,730 disagree. This is an
architectural opportunity count, not a measured cycle or FPGA gain.
The correctly predicted cases can remove a replay bubble; disagreement
must recover at the same absolute cycle as the original waiting branch.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one prediction-led BEQ/BNE dependency bypass. Keep the current
stateless predictor, four-entry fetch queue and ordinary EX resolution.
When decode holds a legal BEQ or BNE whose true rs1/rs2 source
matches the rd of an advancing legal, nontrapping LOAD in EX,
admit that branch into ID/EX instead of inserting the load-use bubble.
Record a deferred-validation bit and a separate pending bit per operand.
Keep every other consumer's interlock, all MUL-use replays and the nret=1
contract unchanged. Signed/unsigned relational branches remain in EX.
A LOAD qualifies only when its effective address is aligned for its width;
derive this eligibility from the forwarded address low bits and validated
decode. A trapping producer must use the original replay behavior.

In EX, a deferred branch follows its captured prediction without resolving
from the producer's unavailable EX/MEM result. Suppress its ordinary EX
condition, correction and taken-target trap decision; MEM alone finalizes
those fields from actual operands. It is never a register or
memory producer. Capture each available source after ordinary forwarding;
carry pending-source bits, equality/inequality sense, PC, direct target, prediction and
precomputed recovery PC into EX/MEM. During a real data-bus hold keep the
branch and its metadata in ID/EX until the older request accepts. Preserve
retained MEM/WB bypass data throughout these holds.

In MEM, validate that deferred branch using the preceding producer's
registered MEM/WB result for each pending operand and the saved EX values
for all other operands. Reuse EX/MEM.multiply_a and multiply_b as the
available functional operand captures: those existing registers already
contain the exact forwarded rs1/rs2 and are idle for a branch. Keep RVFI
metadata separate from the functional validator. The producer and consumer association is fixed
by in-order adjacency; assert the expected nonzero destination and write
eligibility. Resolve equality/inequality and direct-target alignment as
today. With exactly one pending operand, compare WB against the saved
other operand; with both pending, the operands are identical and equality
is true. Use one equality comparator and the BEQ/BNE sense bit, rather
than replicating the full EX signed/unsigned comparator and operation mux.
Select architectural pc_next and RVFI rs1/rs2 data from these actual
operands, never from prediction. The branch retires exactly once with its
ordinary instruction/order fields and the correct trap decision.

A correct prediction allows the younger EX instruction to advance normally.
A late mismatch has priority over younger EX control transfers: squash
that EX slot before EX/MEM capture, DIV launch, forwarding advertisement,
register/memory side effects or retirement; also kill younger ID admission
and flush speculative fetch occupancy. Install the branch's carried direct
recovery PC using the champion's direct recovery mechanism. Suppress every
competing younger redirect/indirect landing. The older producer already
resides in MEM/WB, and the deferred branch has no dmem request, so this
validation cycle cannot have a genuine MEM bus hold. Do not introduce a
stall or extra correction edge for late validation. Reset clears deferred
validity and prevents a stale validation event.

Keep late correction based on registered MEM/WB data, with a small local
comparator and predecoded condition; avoid dmemRData-to-fetch feedback.
The initial branch entered EX one cycle earlier, so validation in MEM
reaches the same correction edge as the existing branch after its replay.
Correct predictions save an issue slot; incorrect predictions must not
increase target-admission latency. Ordinary branches and JAL/JALR retain
their current EX resolution and registered indirect landing behavior.

Preserve all decoder legality checks, alignment traps, arithmetic and
ALTOPS, contiguous retirement order, exact-once effects, memory bounds,
canonical CRCs/UART and marker timing. Directed tests must cover either
pending source and both pending sources, BEQ/BNE and both prediction
outcomes, LOAD widths/signs, older dmem stalls, occupied/full
fetch queues, reset and misaligned producers/targets. Place STORE, LOAD,
DIV/REM, MUL, illegal instructions and JALR in the younger EX slot of a
late miss and prove their effects and launches are suppressed. Verify
actual RVFI source values, recovery PCs, order and latency independently.
Verify that MUL dependencies, reserved branch encodings, relational
branches and trapping producers retain their original replay behavior.
Include an ordinary load-dependent younger branch behind a deferred one:
pending bits must follow the admitted instruction, not a current decode
opcode or a load slot that has already advanced.

Run unchanged lint/unit/formal/cosim gates and canonical stalled CoreMark
plus all three Gowin placements. At 87.715 MHz, even the optimistic
105,590-slot saving gives only about 2.7 percent throughput gain; clearing
the 4.6 percent margin would then need median Fmax above 89.3585 MHz,
about 1.9 percent higher than the champion. Actual savings may be lower
because imem stalls and other holds overlap replay bubbles. The late
validator starts from registered WB and an available-source capture,
avoiding EX forwarding and the six-way branch-condition selection for
this class. It adds only a few metadata bits and one recovery PC, with
existing operand registers reused; it adds no fetch lookup state.
Its comparator and squash fanout can still hurt timing. Expected impact is
low confidence and must be established by measured cycles and vendor timing.
